text:
Stephen Condreay received explicit photographs of a minor victim

LANSING, MICHIGAN – U.S. Attorney for the Western District of Michigan Timothy VerHey today announced that Stephen Condreay, 22, of Braidwood, IL, was sentenced to 5 years in prison for receiving child pornography and was immediately taken into custody by the U.S. Marshal. During the sentencing hearing, Chief U.S. District Judge Hala Y. Jarbou emphasized the serious nature of Condreay’s crimes and the need to protect the public as reasons for the sentence.

Condreay, while an enlisted member of the United States Navy, created a fake Snapchat profile and received explicit photographs from an eleven-year-old victim.

U.S. Attorney Timothy VerHey said he was satisfied with the sentence. “Condreay somehow did not hear the message that people who sexually exploit our children will pay with prison time. He will now have five years to commit it to memory. I appreciate the work that was done by HSI and the Michigan State Police to bring this case to justice.”

“Those entrusted to serve our country are held to the highest standards of conduct,” said HSI Detroit acting Special Agent in Charge Michael Larson. “This sentence holds the defendant accountable for serious crimes involving the exploitation of children. HSI remains steadfast in its commitment to identify and investigate those who seek to harm children, regardless of their position or status, and we are grateful for the critical partnership of HSI Hartford and the Naval Criminal Investigative Service in this case.”

The Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) Sault Ste. Marie office and the Michigan State Police investigated the case.

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys' Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit Justice.gov/PSC .
title: Former U.S. Sailor Sentenced to 60 Months in Prison

HUNTINGTON, W.Va. – Elizabeth Jane Cumper, 46, of Marlette, Michigan, pleaded guilty today to aiding and abetting the distribution of 50 grams or more of a methamphetamine mixture. Cumper admitted to her role in a drug trafficking organization (DTO) that distributed methamphetamine and fentanyl in the Huntington area.

According to court documents and statements made in court, on June 12, 2025, co-defendant William Louis Johnson III sold approximately 389.2 grams of methamphetamine and 1 gram of fentanyl to a confidential informant in exchange for $2,400. As part of her guilty plea, Cumper admitted that she delivered methamphetamine to Johnson for the transaction.

Cumper is scheduled to be sentenced on February 22, 2027, and faces a mandatory minimum of five years and up to 40 years in prison, at least four years of supervised release, and a fine of up to $5 million.

Johnson, also known as “BJ,” 40, of Detroit, Michigan, pleaded guilty on September 28, 2026, to aiding and abetting the distribution of 50 grams or more of a methamphetamine mixture and is scheduled to be sentenced on February 1, 2027. Six other co-defendants pleaded guilty in the case. The indictment remains pending against one co-defendant. An indictment is merely an allegation, and all defendants are presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.

United States Attorney Moore Capito made the announcement and commended the investigative work of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), the Cabell County Sheriff's Office, the Mason County Sheriff’s Office, and the Huntington Police Department, and the assistance provided by the Ohio Highway Patrol and the Marion County, Ohio, Sheriff’s Office.

United States District Judge Robert C. Chambers presided over the hearing. Assistant United States Attorneys Courtney L. Finney and Joseph F. Adams are prosecuting the case.

This case is part of Operation Take Back America , a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime.

A copy of this press release is located on the website of the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of West Virginia. Related court documents and information can be found on PACER by searching for Case No. 3:25-cr-154.

text:
FRESNO, Calif. — Ron Cook, 58, of Fresno, has been indicted on multiple charges of making false statements to the federal government, wire fraud, aggravated identity theft, and money laundering for running a nearly $65 million fraud scheme through his company, Corporate America Lending (CAL), U.S. Attorney Eric Grant announced today.

Cook was arrested at his office this morning and will make his initial court appearance this afternoon.

According to court records, CAL is a lending company based in Fresno that originates loans for farmers, ranchers, and others who work in the agriculture industry. Once CAL originates the loans, it sells the interest in them to others, including investors, financial companies, and the Federal Agricultural Mortgage Company (Farmer MAC). Farmer MAC is a company backed by the federal government that provides increased access to affordable financing for the agriculture industry.

Beginning in 2023, the borrowers of a $58 million loan that Cook had originated and sold to one financial company refinanced the loan with another financial company. The first financial company did not know about the refinancing. Cook then made several misrepresentations to the borrowers, the first financial company, and the second financial company so that he would receive the $58 million refinance amount without the first financial company becoming aware and could keep the money for himself. When the first financial company found out about the refinancing, Cook transferred the money to his friends and associates to conceal its location. It was these transfers that resulted in the money laundering charges.

During this period, Cook also defrauded his other customers and investors. He defrauded his customers by stealing their identities and taking out loans in their names from Farmer MAC without their knowledge, and he defrauded his investors by selling them interests in loans that did not actually exist. It was Cook’s stealing his customers’ identities to get loans from Farmer MAC that resulted in the false statements to the federal government charge against him.

Cook obtained at least $64 million through his fraud scheme. He used the money to pay for his lifestyle and to pay debts that he owed to some of his customers and investors who had detected the fraud and threatened to file criminal charges against him. He also used the money to make political donations.

The Federal Bureau of Investigation conducted the investigation. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Arelis Clemente and Joseph Barton are prosecuting the case.

If convicted, Cook faces 30 years in prison and a $250,000 fine for the making false statements to the federal government charge. He faces 20 years in prison and a fine of up to $250,000 for each of the wire fraud and money laundering charges. Finally, he faces a mandatory two years in prison, consecutive to the sentence he receives for any other charges, for each of the aggravated identity theft charges. Any sentence, however, would be determined at the discretion of the court after consideration of any applicable statutory factors and the federal Sentencing Guidelines, which take into account a number of variables. The charges are only allegations; the defendant is presumed innocent until and unless proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt.

On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (“Fraud Division”). The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.
title: Fresno Executive Indicted for $65 Million Fraud Scheme that Defrauded Farmer MAC and Others

Stamford Man Sentenced to Additional Prison Time for Distributing Crack Prior to Reporting to Prison
STAMFORD, Conn. - David X. Sullivan, United States Attorney for the District of Connecticut, announced that DANNY TURKVAN, also known as “Smooth” 55, of Stamford, has been sentenced by U.S. District Judge Stefan R. Underhill in Bridgeport to an additional 14 months of imprisonment for distributing crack cocaine after he had been sentenced in another federal case and prior to reporting to prison.
On August 13, 2025, Turkvan was sentenced in Hartford federal court to 46 months of imprisonment and three years of supervised release for his participation in a southwestern Connecticut narcotics trafficking conspiracy. Turkvan, who was released on a $150,000 bond, was ordered to report to prison on October 16, 2025. An investigation revealed that Turkvan continued to distribute narcotics after his August 2025 sentencing. Stamford Police arrested Turkvan on state charges on October 11, 2025, and seized crack cocaine that he intended to distribute.
Turkvan has been detained since his arrest. On July 8, 2026, he pleaded guilty in federal court to possession with intent to distribute cocaine base (“crack”).
This investigation was conducted by the Stamford Police Department and the Drug Enforcement Administration. The case was prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Patricia Stolfi Collins.
title: Stamford Man Sentenced to Additional Prison Time for Distributing Crack Prior to Reporting to Prison

text:
Rep. Summer Lee, House Labor Leaders Demand Answers Over Corporate Union-Busting, Enforcement of Federal Transparency Laws
PITTSBURGH, PA – NOVEMBER 2, 2026 — Today, Congresswoman Summer L. Lee (PA-12) joined House Education and Workforce Committee Ranking Member Robert C. “Bobby” Scott (VA-03) and Subcommittee on Health, Employment, Labor, and Pensions Ranking Member Mark DeSaulnier (CA-10) in demanding answers from the Trump Administration over its failure to adequately enforce federal transparency laws governing corporations and union-busting consultants.
In a letter to Office of Labor-Management Standards (OLMS) Director Elisabeth Messenger, the lawmakers raised serious concerns about widespread failures by employers and anti-union consultants to disclose how much money they spend attempting to influence workers' decisions to organize.
Too often, when workers exercise their right to organize a union, corporations and bosses hire outside consultants to wage anti-union campaigns. Over the last several decades, union-avoidance has become a multi-billion-dollar industry. The latest analysis found that companies spend approximately $1.7 billion every year, including nearly $500 million on union-busting consultants, to break their organizing drives. Some consultants are reportedly paid $500 per hour or $4,000 per day for their services.
Under the Labor-Management Reporting and Disclosure Act (LMRDA), employers and consultants are required to file public reports about their matter because it allows workers to see how much their bosses are spending to influence their decision to unionize. However, for decades, employers and union-busting consultants have routinely failed to meet this requirement, allowing bosses and their consultants to operate in the shadows. Under the Trump Administration, the problem is only becoming worse. A recent watchdog report found that, as of August 8, 2026, nearly 60 percent of employers required to file a disclosure in 2025 have still not submitted their reports—the largest year-over-year decline on record.
“Over the last several years, while worker organizing has skyrocketed, employers have increasingly responded with hostile anti-union campaigns, including by hiring well-compensated outside consultants. As more employers seek to quash their workers’ unionization drives, it is imperative that employer and consultant disclosure requirements under the LMRDA are robustly enforced by OLMS, so workers have a complete picture of who is attempting to influence their decision as they exercise their right to organize,” wrote the Members.
To determine whether OLMS is effectively carrying out its responsibility to enforce the LMRDA, the Members requested a response to their extensive questions by no later than November 16, 2026.
To read the full letter to OLMS Director Elisabeth Messenger, click here.
Congresswoman Summer Lee serves on the House Committee on Judiciary and the Committee on Education and Workforce. Since taking office in January 2023, she has delivered historic levels of federal investment totaling over $2.7 Billion brought back to Western PA, including over $580 million for infrastructure, over $110 million for affordable transit, over $500 million to keep clean energy manufacturing at home in Pennsylvania, and over $55 million on clean energy efforts in and around schools to help keep our kids and communities safe. These investments will help improve Western Pennsylvania’s infrastructure and transit, ensure cleaner air and drinking water, lower housing costs, fund research institutions, fuel clean manufacturing, fund STEM innovation and entrepreneurship, boost workforce development, and create thousands of good paying union jobs. Lee and her team have also delivered casework and constituent services to over 4,000 constituents with issues ranging from helping our seniors and disabled community access Medicare and social security to helping folks secure housing and helping families with immigration support and passports.
title: Rep. Summer Lee, House Labor Leaders Demand Answers Over Corporate Union-Busting, Enforcement of Federal Transparency Laws

Secretary Kennedy Advances MAHA in Michigan and Iowa with Focus on Nutrition, Recovery, and Maternal Health
WASHINGTON, D.C.—NOVEMBER 2, 2026— U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. advanced President Trump's Make America Healthy Again agenda last week during four days of stops in Michigan and Iowa on his "Take Back Your Health Tour." Secretary Kennedy celebrated more than 250 hospitals committing to healthier food, highlighted a $12 million investment in Detroit's treatment and recovery services, and announced new infant formula actions to support growing families.
"Under President Trump's leadership, we are bringing real food into hospitals, investing in addiction recovery, and helping mothers give their children a healthy start," said Secretary Kennedy. "In Michigan and Iowa, I met people turning these priorities into action. HHS is backing their work to Make America Healthy Again."
On October 26, Secretary Kennedy visited Corewell Health's Lifestyle and Culinary Medicine Practice in Grand Rapids, Michigan, for a roundtable, tour, and cooking demonstration. He met with healthcare leaders, clinicians, and culinary medicine professionals to discuss how hospitals can serve healthier meals and give patients practical skills to continue eating well at home. During the visit, Secretary Kennedy celebrated more than 250 hospitals signing the Make Hospital Food Healthier Pledge. The visit also highlighted Corewell Health's work to connect clinical care with cooking instruction, nutrition education, and community programs.
"As part of our commitment to make health better, Corewell Health supports HHS' Make Hospital Food Healthier Pledge, which builds on work we have been doing for years to improve the meals we serve our patients. We appreciated the recent visit from the Secretary which showcased our focus on serving whole foods, cutting back on sugar and sodium and using healthier cooking methods. Nutrition is an important part of patient care, which we train our current and future physicians to incorporate. The right food choices are always guided by conversations between patients, physicians and their care teams," said Tina Freese Decker, Corewell Health president and CEO.
On October 27, Secretary Kennedy toured Detroit Wayne Integrated Health Network's crisis care facility and joined a roundtable with city officials, healthcare providers, faith leaders, and Americans who confronted addiction and embraced the path of recovery. The visit highlighted Detroit's selection as one of eight communities receiving funding through the HHS STREETS program. The Detroit Health Department will receive $12 million over four years to establish its Prevention and Access to Treatment, Housing, and Stability program, known as PATHS. Through coordinated outreach and services, PATHS will connect people experiencing homelessness and serious mental illness, substance use disorders, or both with treatment, recovery support, and stable housing.
"We are grateful to the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services and its Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration for recognizing the urgent needs of our community. This STREETS funding strengthens DWIHN's ability to connect people experiencing homelessness and co-occurring mental health and substance use disorders with the treatment and support they need to move toward recovery, stability, and independence," said James E. White, President and CEO, Detroit Wayne Integrated Health Network (DWIHN).
Secretary Kennedy also announced new analysis from the HHS Office of the Assistant Secretary for Planning and Evaluation highlighting how actions across President Trump's two terms to reduce unnecessary opioid prescribing, combat illicit fentanyl, and strengthen treatment and recovery have led opioid-related deaths in the United States to plummet to the lowest since President Trump declared a public health emergency in 2017.
On October 28, Secretary Kennedy, joined by Kathryn Burgum and HHS Center for Faith Director Monty Burks, visited Sheepgate in Colfax, Iowa. The trio toured the residential recovery facility, met with program leaders, and engaged with clients sharing their journeys from addiction to sobriety. The discussion focused on faith-based recovery, mentoring, and helping people return to their families and communities. Sheepgate's structured program combines Biblical teaching, fellowship, practical work experience, and support for re-entry. The visit highlighted the role of faith and community partnerships in advancing President Trump's Great American Recovery.
"Addiction affects so much more than the person struggling. It impacts families and entire communities. For more than 50 years at Sheepgate, a division of Adult and Teen Challenge of the Midlands, we've seen firsthand how Jesus Christ can completely transform lives. We were grateful for the opportunity to welcome Secretary Kennedy, Kathryn Burgum and Monty Burks to share what's working in faith-based recovery and discuss the challenges we face. As we fight this crisis together, our hope is to build stronger partnerships and make sure finances never stand in the way of someone getting the help they need," said Michael Hunsberger, President of Sheepgate.
Secretary Kennedy concluded the trip on October 29 at Everystep in West Des Moines, Iowa, where he joined Health Resources and Services Administration Administrator Tom Engels for a maternal health roundtable. During the visit, Secretary Kennedy delivered a Newborn Essentials Support Toolkit (NEST) to an expectant mother and announced new FDA actions on infant formula including proposed updates to nutrient requirements and an online dashboard giving families easier access to formula information.
"Every child and their family deserves access to the care and support they need to be healthy and thrive," said Tray Wade, president and CEO of EveryStep. "At EveryStep, we have seen firsthand the difference maternal and child health programs have made for Iowa families, from supporting healthy pregnancies to helping parents navigate the challenges of raising young children. We were honored to have welcomed Secretary Kennedy and national health care leaders to share the important work happening in our communities and discuss why continued state and federal support remains so important to the families who rely on these services."
Together, these visits underscored the Trump Administration's commitment to healthier food, lasting recovery, and stronger families — turning national priorities into practical support in communities across America.

Justice Department Announces Charges Involving 63 Individuals for Election-Related Crimes
Today, the Justice Department announced charges involving 63 individuals, including four illegal aliens, in connection with illegal voting, fraudulent voter registration, and related election crimes across the country. The cases include voting by aliens in federal elections, false claims of U.S. citizenship to register to vote or to vote, and the fraudulent submission of a voter registration application in another state.
“Today’s announcement marks the largest surge of voter-fraud arrests since President Trump returned to office,” said Attorney General Todd Blanche. “These foreign nationals allegedly took advantage of the trust of the American people and flouted the laws that govern our nation’s elections. This Department of Justice will continue investigating and prosecuting voter fraud to restore confidence in our electoral system.”
In the last nine weeks alone, the Department has charged 195 aliens across 25 states with illegal voting and registration offenses. Since the beginning of this Administration, we have charged 239 people with voting fraud-related offenses.
Case details are as follows:
Northern District of Georgia
Benito Covarrubias Iniguez, 64, an illegal alien from Mexico has been charged with making a false claim of U.S. citizenship in order to vote in a federal election.
Southern District of Texas
Five aliens, including an illegal alien, have been charged with election-related crimes.
- Ali Khan, 33, an illegal alien from the Republic of Trinidad and Tobago, has been charged with voting by an alien. Khan allegedly voted in the 2024 election.
- Nigerian national Mohammed Omar Hassan, 61, a lawful permanent resident, has been charged with voting by an alien. Hassan allegedly voted in the 2022 and 2024 elections.
- Mexican national Diego Benavides Rodriguez, 29, a lawful permanent resident, has been charged with voting by an alien and an additional charge of falsely claiming U.S. citizenship.
- Mexican national Jose Vasquez-Mendoza, 51, a lawful permanent resident, has been charged with voting by an alien. Vasquez-Mendoza allegedly voted in the 2022 special election for Congressional District 34.
- Mexican national Karen Hinojosa-Martinez, 37, a lawful permanent resident, has been charged with lying on immigration documents after allegedly voting in a federal election.
District of Maryland
Mohammad Hachibur Rahman, 33, an illegal alien from Bangladesh, is charged by information with unlawful voting. Rahman allegedly voted in the November 2024 election. The election was held in part for the purpose of selecting a candidate for president, vice president, or member of the U.S. Senate or House of Representatives.
Eastern District of North Carolina
Nine aliens, including an illegal alien, have been charged with election-related crimes.
- Selvin Porfidio Gonzalez Escobar, 43, an illegal alien from Guatemala living in Robeson County, North Carolina, is charged with one count of falsely claiming citizenship to vote and one count of voting by an alien. He registered to vote in 2020 and voted in the 2024 and 2020 general elections.

Crudup allegedly registered to vote in 2008 and voted in nine general elections in 2024, 2022, 2020, 2018, 2016, 2014, 2012, 2010, and 2008, as well as nine primary elections in 2026, 2024, 2022, 2020, 2018, 2016, 2014, 2010, and 2008.

Middle District of North Carolina
Five aliens have been charged with election-related crimes.

Three aliens have been charged with election-related crimes.

Western District of Tennessee
Two aliens have been charged with voting by an alien.
- Mexican national Cesar Sanchez Correa, 44, a lawful permanent resident, has been charged with one count of unlawful voting by an alien. Sanchez Correa allegedly illegally voted in Haywood County, TN in the 2024 election held in part for the purpose of electing a candidate for President, Vice President, Member of the U.S. Senate, or Member of the U.S. House of Representatives, and allegedly falsely and willfully represented himself to be a citizen of the United States in a Tennessee voter registration application in order to vote in a federal, state, or local election.

Van Der Werf allegedly illegally voted in Fayette County, TN in both the 2022 and 2024 elections held in part for the purpose of electing a candidate for President, Vice President, Member of the U.S. Senate, or Member of the U.S. House of Representatives, and allegedly falsely and willfully represented himself to be a citizen of the United States in a Tennessee voter registration application in order to vote in a federal, state, or local election.
Eastern District of Tennessee
Two aliens have been charged with illegally voting.
- Iraqi national Mark Adwar Odisho, 30, a lawful permanent resident, has been charged with illegally voting in the U.S. presidential election on Nov. 5, 2024. He made his initial appearance in federal court on Oct.29.
- French national Frederic Jean Rene Sicard, 50, a lawful permanent resident, has been charged with illegally voting in the U.S. presidential election on Nov. 5, 2024. He made his initial appearance in federal court on Oct. 30, 2026.
District of New Jersey
Two aliens have been charged with election-related crimes.
- Jamaican national Antonio Mitchell, 54, a lawful permanent resident, has been charged with voting by an alien and unlawfully attempting to procure U.S. citizenship. Mitchell has also been charged with an additional count of making false statements while applying for U.S. citizenship. Mitchell allegedly voted in-person in the 2022 general election. Mitchell falsely claimed that he had never registered to vote or voted in any federal elections. Additionally, after submitting his application for naturalization (N-400), Mitchell was interviewed by an Immigration Services Officer. In that interview and while under oath, Mitchell denied having registered to vote, or having voted, in any federal election.
- Italian national Andrea Morzetta, 72, a lawful permanent resident, has been charged with voting by an alien and unlawfully attempting to procure U.S. citizenship. Morzetta allegedly voted in-person in the November 2024 general election and falsely claimed that he had never registered to vote or voted in any federal elections when applying for U.S. citizenship.
Western District of Wisconsin

JOINT BASE SAN ANTONIO-FORT SAM HOUSTON, Texas – Brooke Army Medical Center participated in the annual San Antonio Mass Casualty Exercise and Evaluation Oct. 21 to test the hospital’s emergency preparedness and response capabilities in case of a mass casualty incident.
SAMCEE is designed to assess the surge capabilities of hospitals in the 26,000-square-mile region covered by the Southwest Texas Regional Advisory Council. The exercise specifically covers participating hospitals’ treatment processes, patient tracking abilities, and family reunification procedures.
“As one of two Level 1 trauma centers, we not only treat military members and their beneficiaries, but also civilian trauma patients,” Emergency Manager George Wible said. “So, if there ever was a mass casualty incident, BAMC will be one of the primary recipients of patients.”
As part of the simulated drill, BAMC physicians, nurses, medical personnel and staff received news via mass text shortly after 8 a.m. that a mid-air collision had been reported near San Antonio International Airport. Soon after, about 55 “victims,” or volunteer role players, began arriving at BAMC in emergency vehicles with various life-threatening mock injuries.
Army Lt. Col. (Dr.) Michael Rowland, trauma medical director, said the Trauma Department’s participation in the exercise each year is vital. “By treating patients through a variety of emergency scenarios, the exercise allows our trauma surgeons to provide quality care for critically injured patients should an incident ever happen,” he said.
One role player, Army Pvt. Angelina Doss, portrayed a 9-year-old who arrived at the emergency room with severe chest pain and breathing problems. Emergency physicians diagnosed her with a collapsed lung after conducting medical tests.
“It was a lot of fun,” she said. “I liked the staging area where they put the moulage (simulated injuries) on us, and then coming in and seeing how the entire hospital was involved to prepare for an actual emergency.”
BAMC was one of 50 hospitals and healthcare facilities in the region to participate in SAMCEE.
Air Force Col. Amy Brown, deputy commander of surgical services, who executed her role in the Hospital Command Center along with other key leadership, said BAMC takes an “all-hands on deck approach” while conducting the disaster drill.
“Disaster response is directed by the hospital incident commander with additional team members having assigned roles and areas of responsibility,” Brown said. “We have playbooks that allow for dynamic collaboration between departments such as the ED (Emergency Department), Logistics, Facilities, Public Affairs, OR (Operating Room), Manpower, and Patient Registration. Security, Mental Health and Chaplain services play a vital role in assisting families separated from victims and providing reunification.”
Army Capt. Cristina Western, dietitian, volunteered to be an observer/controller and was responsible for tracking patient movements from point of entry to placement in an inpatient unit. She also noted any procedures that could be improved on.
“I didn’t realize how widespread across San Antonio that SAMCEE was and how many external entities were involved,” Western said. “It was eye-opening to see what the whole process involves.”
According to STRAC, the South Texas medical community uses a four-pronged approach to emergency preparedness: plan, equip, train, and exercise. Results from the exercise are used to improve emergency plans, identify equipment shortages, and other areas for improvement.
After the four-hour exercise ended, Wible provided an early assessment of the simulated drill.
“I’ve heard positive remarks that things went a lot more smoothly and effectively than previous exercises,” he said. “Of course, not everything went flawlessly. Ultimately, what we hope to have accomplished is that we identify any gaps or inconsistencies that we can improve upon. We will take those lessons learned and put them into a revised plan, and when we do it again, hopefully we will do even better.”
title: BAMC tests emergency readiness, patient influx capabilities during mass casualty exercise

CINCINNATI – U.S. Attorney Dominick S. Gerace II announced today results of the Southern District of Ohio’s continuing work to reduce violent crime, firearms offenses and fraud in fiscal year 2026.

Fiscal year 2026 includes Oct. 1, 2025, through Sept. 30, 2026.

Violent and Gun Crime

“I am extremely proud of what my Office has accomplished since I became U.S. Attorney just over a year ago,” said U.S. Attorney Gerace. “My tenure began amid a significant uptick in violent and gun crimes, particularly in downtown Cincinnati, and I promised the public that we would aggressively pursue federal charges against those offenders. The statistics show that we have done just that. I asked my prosecutors to target repeat violent offenders and to focus on the safety of the streets in our communities and they continue to answer the bell.”

As indicated below, in Cincinnati alone, the Office increased prosecutions of firearms offenders by 250% when compared to FY2025. More generally, violent crime prosecutions increased by 148.5% in Cincinnati and by 92.7% districtwide.

The total number of defendants charged with firearms offenses and violent crimes across the District sets a Southern District of Ohio record based on available statistics going back to FY2004. The total number of defendants charged with firearms offenses represents an increase of 93.5% from FY2025.

Defendants Charged with Violent Crimes

Defendants Charged with Firearms Offenses (18 U.S.C. 922(g) and 924(c))

“None of these cases are possible without strong partnerships with our local, state and federal law enforcement agencies who investigate these crimes. I thank them for joining us in the fight against violence,” said U.S. Attorney Gerace. “I am also grateful to Ohio Attorney General Andy Wilson for his continued support and for providing us with a Special Assistant United States Attorney dedicated to federal gun cases.”

Fraud and White-Collar Crime

“The fight against fraud, especially fraud against taxpayer-funded government benefits programs, is a top priority for this Office,” said U.S. Attorney Gerace. “This fiscal year, we brought charges against several individuals who allegedly stole tens of millions of dollars from government programs designed to provide healthcare and food benefits to Americans in need—including a Medicaid fraud scheme involving $30 million and a SNAP fraud scheme involving $29.7 million. We will continue to hold fraudsters accountable for stealing taxpayer dollars and for depriving vulnerable citizens of these services.”

As indicated below, the District increased prosecution of white-collar defendants by 46.3% when compared to FY2025, with the largest increases coming from the Dayton and Columbus areas.

Defendants Charged with White-Collar Crimes

“These statistics represent just a few of the areas that our dedicated public servants focus on every day to keep the people of the Southern District of Ohio safe,” added U.S. Attorney Gerace. “In addition to violent, gun and white-collar crime, my Office remains steadfast in combatting child exploitation, protecting our homeland security, ridding our streets of deadly drugs, enforcing immigration laws, and dismantling transnational criminal organizations. We are proud to do our jobs in service to our communities and this great country.”

# # #
title: U.S. Attorney Gerace announces FY2026 prosecution statistics

The Air Force Research Laboratory and Air Combat Command’s Experimental Operations Unit recently flew the XQ-67A Autonomous Collaborative Platform in the Nevada Test and Training Range marking a technology milestone in autonomous capabilities for the future fight.
The flight, which was completed under the Demonstration of ACP Performance and Effectiveness project, directly supports National Defense Strategy priorities for the Department of the Air Force by accelerating ACP development and delivery.
“By pairing AFRL’s rapid prototyping with ACC's operational test units, the Air Force is shortening the timeline between concept and warfighter capability,” said Col. Matthew Caspers, DAF Deputy Technology Executive Officer for Air.
During the flight, the XQ-67A demonstrated integration of several advanced mission systems, including state-of-the-art sensors, mission computers, and power and thermal management hardware, all designed to work collaboratively in demanding combat environments.
Additionally, the integration of Beyond Line-of-Sight datalinks and live, virtual and constructive simulations during the flight demonstrated management of uncrewed platforms across distributed theaters, bolstering deterrence through resilient, layered command and control.
“This proved that AFRL’s autonomous architectures, aligned with Autonomy and Agile Mission Suite Government Reference Architectures, can reliably process and relay combat-relevant data in real-world scenarios,” said Trenton White, aerospace engineer in AFRL’s Air Warfare directorate.
The research and development investment in unified platforms like the XQ-67A validates how uncrewed systems can extend the operational reach of crewed fighter formations. It provides solutions for equipping commanders with deep situational awareness and adding affordable operational mass to the fleet, all while significantly reducing risk to human aircrews.
About AFRL
The Air Force Research Laboratory is the Department of the Air Force’s primary scientific research and development center and one of six centers within Air Force Materiel Command. AFRL leads the discovery, development and delivery of technologies for air, space and multidomain operations. With a workforce spanning seven mission areas at more than 40 locations worldwide, AFRL conducts research ranging from basic science to advanced technology development. For more information, visit afresearchlab.com.
title: Air Force Research Laboratory completes flight of XQ-67A, advancing autonomous technology

LAREDO, Texas–U.S. Customs and Border Protection, Homeland Security Investigations, the Drug Enforcement Administration, and the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of Texas announced major enforcement results from Operation Southern Surge, a coordinated Homeland Security Task Force initiative targeting drug trafficking and other cross-border criminal activity.
At a Nov. 2 press conference at the Juarez-Lincoln International Bridge, officials highlighted the operation’s early results and reaffirmed their commitment to stopping dangerous narcotics, weapons, and illicit proceeds before they reach American communities.
Since Oct. 19, Operation Southern Surge has resulted in the seizure of more than 1,600 pounds of narcotics, 15 firearms, more than 3,000 rounds of ammunition, and over $360,000 in illicit currency. These enforcement actions have also led to 89 arrests.
Among the significant enforcement actions under Operation Southern Surge are:
Hidalgo Port of Entry - After a K-9 alert, officers discovered cylindrical packages hidden among a shipment of leeks. A total of 909 packages were discovered and tested positive for methamphetamine. The total weight of the narcotics was 1,082.47 pounds with a street value of $984,063.
Juarez-Lincoln Bridge - CBP officers recently referred a vehicle for secondary inspection. Using nonintrusive inspection technology and their training and experience, an anomaly was detected and officers discovered 49.3 pounds of cocaine concealed in 20 packages.
The officials present at the news conference reiterated that these numbers represent more than enforcement statistics and further reflect the commitment of CBP personnel and law enforcement partners to stop dangerous drugs, weapons, and criminal proceeds from entering our communities.
“Operation Southern Surge leverages tactical intelligence and coordinated enforcement actions to dismantle the trafficking infrastructure, intercept illicit supply chains, and bolster situational awareness across the southwest border,” said Director Jennifer De La O of the Laredo Field Office, Office of Field Operations. “International drug trafficking presents a direct threat to U.S. national security, public safety and economic stability and our partnerships are a force multiplier in detecting these crimes and protecting the public.”
“Securing the border requires more than making seizures or stopping a single smuggling attempt. HSI’s role is to follow the evidence, identify the people behind these crimes, and dismantle the organizations moving drugs, weapons, money, and people across the border,” said Acting Deputy Special Agent in Charge Charles Kerby, HSI Laredo. “Through the Homeland Security Task Force, we are working closely with CBP, DEA, the FBI, and our law enforcement partners to hold these criminal networks accountable and protect communities across the country.”
Under the leadership of President Donald J. Trump and Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, the dedicated men and women of U.S. Customs and Border Protection, alongside our law enforcement partners and with the support of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF), are combating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and drug trafficking networks.
The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership that coordinates law enforcement efforts to identify, investigate, and prosecute these organizations and the crimes they commit in the United States and abroad. The HSTF prioritizes combating child trafficking and other crimes involving children, while supporting efforts to investigate, prosecute, and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States.
Click here for more photos of Operation Southern Surge.
title: CBP, HSI, DEA, USAO in Coordination with the Homeland Security Task Force Tout Successes of Major Drug, Weapons and Cash Seizures in Operation Southern Surge

WASHINGTON — Today, Ambassador Jamieson Greer issued a statement following President Trump notifying Congress and the governments of Rwanda and South Africa of his intent to terminate these countries from the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA) trade preference program, as of January 1, 2027.
“The Office of the United States Trade Representative led the annual interagency review of sub-Saharan African countries’ eligibility for the AGOA trade preference program. Based on the review, President Trump found that the governments of Rwanda and South Africa are engaging in practices that are inconsistent with AGOA’s eligibility criteria,” said Ambassador Greer. “These concerning and pervasive practices include, but are not limited to, barriers that undermine American trade and investment and practices that pose a threat to U.S. national security and foreign policy interests in the region. The Trump Administration is working to ensure our African partners take the necessary steps to meet the eligibility criteria.”
Background:
In Rwanda, the Trump Administration is deeply concerned by the following issues: trade and investment barriers, rule of law, political pluralism, internationally recognized worker rights, human rights, and threats to U.S. national security and foreign policy interests. In South Africa, the Trump Administration is deeply concerned by barriers to U.S. trade and investment, corruption, and threats to U.S. national security and foreign policy interests.
###
title: Ambassador Greer Issues Statement on President Trump’s Intent to Terminate Rwanda and South Africa from the AGOA Trade Preference Program

PICATINNY ARSENAL, N.J. - Picatinny Arsenal’s Family and Morale, Welfare and Recreation Directorate celebrated the grand opening of The Picatinny Lodge on Oct. 28, marking the return of a dedicated gathering space designed to strengthen community, camaraderie and quality-of-life opportunities for Arsenal residents, employees, and their guests.
Located in the space formerly known as Bucky’s, The Picatinny Lodge has been reimagined as a welcoming venue for social events, networking, informal gatherings and private functions.
The facility originally opened in 2008 as Bucky’s, an initiative intended to provide a lunchtime eatery and after-work gathering place for the Picatinny community. Although the venue operated for approximately 10 years and hosted a variety of entertainment concepts, participation did not reach the level needed to sustain operations. Bucky’s closed in fiscal year 2019.
“The effects of the COVID-19 pandemic and increased remote-work practices left the facility largely unused for the next several years,” said Andrew Ciccolella, Picatinny’s FMWR Director.
In 2026, following the arrival of Picatinny Arsenal’s new commanding general who provided a vision for the space, FMWR began planning for the renovation and reopening of the facility in support of the command’s priority to create a new community gathering place and improve quality-of-life amenities across the installation.
“We thought it was important you, the Picatinny employees, have a place to gather and to celebrate the work that you do,” said Maj. Gen. Christopher D. Schneider, Portfolio Acquisition Executive Agile Sustainment and Ammunition and the Picatinny Arsenal Commanding General.“There’s no better place to do that than at a facility that was in disrepair, falling apart, and looking over this beautiful lake. We challenged the MWR team to come up with a vision so that everybody can use it for themselves, their families, friends, industry partners, sponsors; a place where we can all gather and have a good time.”
Renovation work began June 4 and was completed in time for the Oct. 28 grand opening.
“The project moved from concept to opening in only a few months, a timeline that would normally require about a year for a renovation of this scope,” said Ciccolella.
The accelerated effort was made possible through sponsor support, work performed by the Picatinny Garrison Directorate of Public Works, and the sustained efforts of FMWR employees.
The Picatinny Lodge offers indoor and outdoor spaces intended to accommodate a range of uses, including:
- An outdoor fire-pit area with capacity for up to 40 people
- An outdoor deck with capacity for up to 50 people
- Interior seating and gathering space for up to 60 people
- Non-classified Internet Protocol Router Network (NIPRNet) and commercial Wi-Fi
- Three smart televisions with satellite television service
- A full-service bar area
- Catering packages for private events and facility rentals
While the venue has a new identity and service model, it retains ties to its history as Bucky’s. Visitors will find references to the original facility throughout the Lodge, including a dedication plaque, a photo wall and a signature drink named in Bucky’s honor.
The rebranding was an important part of the reopening effort. FMWR determined that the venue’s expanded amenities, revised operating hours and new service style called for a name that better represented its renewed purpose.
The Picatinny Lodge will operate under a membership model intended to help sustain the facility, support extended operating hours and maintain competitive food and beverage pricing. FMWR also expects the membership structure to encourage stewardship of the venue, increase attendance at programs and special events, expand networking opportunities and cultivate a club-like environment centered on shared ownership and community participation.
With its reopening, The Picatinny Lodge provides Picatinny Arsenal with a renewed destination for residents, employees and guests to gather, celebrate and strengthen the connections that support the installation community.
Membership registration can be completed in-person at the MWR Leisure Travel Services office in the Visitor Center. For questions about membership, please contact us at usarmy.mwrpicatinnyguestservices@army.mil.
title: Picatinny Lodge grand opening revitalizes former Bucky’s venue

RELEASE: Gottheimer Claws Back $450K from Washington for Englewood’s Dispatch and Emergency Management Center
Funding Will Finish Construction and Equip Departments with Technology for Centralized Emergency Response for Police, Fire, and EMS
Above: Gottheimer announces clawed-back funds in Englewood for Dispatch and Emergency Management Center.
ENGLEWOOD, NJ — Today, Monday, November 2, 2026, Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) announced that he secured $450,000 in federal funding from Washington for the City of Englewood to invest in the completion of its new Dispatch and Emergency Management Center.
Watch full remarks here and facility tour footage here.
“This funding finishes the construction and fits out the technology, so this center can go live. That means the police chief, the fire chief, and our other partners can sit together and run the response to a major storm, fire, or other incident,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5).
The funding will complete construction of the center and fit it out with the technology it needs to go live. Once operational, police, fire, EMS, and city officials will be able to work off the same information in real time during a major storm, fire, or evacuation, with the people making decisions in the same room as the people talking to units on the ground.
Since coming to Congress, Gottheimer has also clawed back $4,099,061 in federal funding for Englewood’s firefighters, including $739,931 through the Assistance to Firefighters Grant (AFG) program and $3,359,129 through the Staffing for Adequate Fire and Emergency Response (SAFER) program.
Gottheimer was joined by Bergen County Commissioner Tracy Zur, Englewood Mayor Michael Wildes, Councilwoman Dr. Lisa Wisotsky, Police Chief Thomas Greeley, Deputy Police Chief Matthew De La Rosa, Fire Chief Jeffrey Kaplan, Deputy Fire Chief Kyle Hummel, and City Manager Robert Hoffmann.

WASHINGTON — The U.S. Small Business Administration is reminding eligible businesses, private nonprofit organizations, and residents in Washington of the Nov. 23 deadline to apply for low-interest federal disaster loans to offset physical damage caused by the Chelan Hills wildfire occurring July 4 – 10.
The declaration covers the Washington counties of Chelan, Douglas, Grant, Kittitas, and Okanogan.
Businesses and nonprofits are eligible to apply for physical disaster loans and may borrow up to $2 million to repair or replace disaster-damaged or destroyed real estate, machinery, and equipment, inventory, and other business assets.
Homeowners and renters are eligible to apply for home and personal property loans and may borrow up to $100,000 to replace or repair personal property, such as clothing, furniture, cars, and appliances. Homeowners may apply for up to $500,000 to replace or repair their primary residence.
Applicants may also be eligible for a loan increase of up to 20% of their physical damage, as verified by SBA, for mitigation purposes. Eligible mitigation improvements may include strengthening structures to protect against fire damage, upgrading to wind rated garage doors, and installing a safe room or storm shelter to help protect property and occupants from future damage.
“One distinct advantage of SBA’s disaster loan program is the opportunity to fund upgrades reducing the risk of future damage,” said Chris Stallings, Associate Administrator of the Office of Disaster Recovery at SBA. “I encourage businesses and homeowners to work with contractors and mitigation professionals to improve their disaster readiness while taking advantage of our physical damage loans.”
The SBA’s Economic Injury Disaster Loan program is available to eligible small businesses, small agricultural cooperatives, and private nonprofit organizations — including faith-based organizations — impacted by financial losses directly related to this disaster. The SBA is unable to provide disaster loans to agricultural producers, farmers, or ranchers, except for aquaculture enterprises.
Interest rates can be as low as 4% for businesses, 3.625% for nonprofits, and 2.875% for homeowners and renters with terms up to 30 years. Interest does not begin to accrue, and payments are not due until 12 months from the date of the first loan disbursement. The SBA determines eligibility and sets loan amounts and terms based on each applicant’s financial condition.
To apply online, visit sba.gov/disaster. Applicants may also call SBA’s National Support Network Center at (866) SBA-HELP or email disastercustomerservice@sba.gov for more information on SBA disaster assistance. For people who are deaf, hard of hearing, or have a speech disability, please dial 7-1-1 to access telecommunications relay services.
The filing deadline to submit applications for physical damage is Nov. 23. However, after the deadline has passed, there is a 60-day grace period in which SBA will accept applications. The deadline to return economic injury applications is June 22, 2027.
###
About the U.S. Small Business Administration
The U.S. Small Business Administration helps power the American dream of business ownership. As the only go-to resource and voice for small businesses backed by the strength of the federal government, the SBA empowers entrepreneurs and small business owners with the resources and support they need to start, grow, expand their businesses, or recover from a declared disaster. It delivers services through an extensive network of SBA field offices and partnerships with public and private organizations. To learn more, visit www.sba.gov.
title: SBA Relief Still Available to Washington Businesses, Private Nonprofits, Residents Affected by the Chelan Hills Wildfire

The Federal Maritime Commission (FMC) will host a research symposium on March 31, 2027, at its headquarters in Washington, D.C. This event will bring together scholars conducting research on demurrage and detention (DnD) practices and policies, as well as industry experts who will share insights regarding the use of DnD to incentivize cargo fluidity and velocity.
The symposium will foster research and discussion that can advance the understanding of DnD practices and their broader economic and operational implications for freight fluidity. The symposium will focus on the following overarching research question: What economic theories or quantifiable frameworks can be developed and used to evaluate the relationships among compensatory costs, DnD charge levels, and the behavioral responses necessary to effectively incentivize cargo movement and freight fluidity?
The FMC is now accepting submission from individuals interested in sharing their papers examining the policies and effects of DnD. The Commission especially encourages the submission of papers that develop and/or evaluate methodologies for setting DnD charges above compensatory costs in order to maintain and demonstrate an effective incentive. Papers may also develop or examine methodologies to assess behavioral responses to DnD charges and how those responses can be deployed to improve cargo velocity and freight fluidity.
Key dates
- Deadline for submissions – February 15, 2027
- Notification to author(s) – March 1, 2027
- Registration opens and agenda announced – March 1, 2027
- Research symposium – March 31, 2027
The research symposium will focus on the following key themes and questions:
Overall incentivizing mechanism:
- Establish a quantifiable economic framework for determining whether, and by how much, DnD charges must differ from actual compensatory costs to effectively incentivize the desired behavioral responses.
- Identify controllable and uncontrollable factors associated with DnD and evaluate how these factors affect charge levels, compensatory costs, and incentive effectiveness.
DnD charges:
- What factors impact the effectiveness of DnD charges as financial incentives?
- Examine how DnD terms and rates are negotiated and determine how contractual relationships, the Incoterms, and/or government holds influence the level and structure of DnD charges.
- Examine decision-making alignment across relevant parties, including whether the party that controls the relevant operational behavior is consistently the party that bears the financial consequences of DnD charges.
Compensatory costs:
- How should compensatory costs associated with DnD be identified, measured, and quantified?
- How can one deploy a quantifiable framework for compensatory costs, including actual costs and opportunity costs, associated with DnD and identify the factors that influence those costs?
Behavioral changes:
- What is the demonstrated relationship between increases in DnD charges and incremental improvements in the desired behavior, and at what point do diminishing returns occur?
- Examine how behavioral responses to DnD incentives translate into improvements in cargo velocity and overall freight fluidity.
If you are interested in submitting a paper, please send an executive summary, extended abstract, or completed paper by February 15, 2027, to Grace Wang at WWang@fmc.gov. You will receive an email confirming receipt of your submission. Preference to participate in the symposium will be given to completed papers.
Accepted participants should expect to receive notification by March 1, 2027. For those interested in attending the conference as audience members, registration will open March 1, 2027. This symposium will be held at FMC Headquarters: 800 North Capitol Street, N.W. Washington, D.C., 20573. For more information or questions, please contact Grace Wang at WWang@fmc.gov and Melina Reilly at MReilly@fmc.gov.

The Army has conducted ceremonies throughout its history to celebrate special occasions, like a new commander taking the reins of a unit.
Brig. Gen. Jeremy Wilson assumed command of the Army Training Center and Fort Jackson in one such ceremony held Oct. 30 at Victory Field on post.
“Thank you for being here today as we welcome the Wilson family to Fort Jackson,” said Lt. Gen. Johnny K. Davis, commander of the U.S. Army Recruiting Command, who presided over the ceremony. “I want to recognize Brig. Gen. Jeremy Wilson’s incredible family, his wife Marti, their children and the loved ones here with us today.”
The ceremony marked the placing of trust on the shoulders “of a proven combat leader, an exceptional trainer, and a leader of character who understands what it takes to build readiness from the ground up,” Davis said.
Davis added Wilson has his total confidence.
“You’ve got an incredible team of superstars behind you, and I know … you’re going to crush it,” he said.
Commanding a unit like the Army Training Center takes a commitment from the whole family, said Davis, who leads the organization that runs the Army’s force generation pipeline.
It is “a team sport and a family commitment,” he said while welcoming the Wilsons to the team. “We know Jeremy wouldn’t do it; wouldn’t be standing here without the strength and love behind him from this great family.”
Wilson, who started his Army career as an armor officer upon graduation from the Citadel in 1996, said he is “humbled and honored” to take command.
“Fort Jackson holds a special place in our Army,” he said during the ceremony. “Our mission is fundamental to America’s national defense. Bottom line, we make American Soldiers. Every day young men and women arrive here as civilians to begin their transformation into disciplined, capable, members of our profession.
“The responsibility we carry is profound, and the standard we uphold must always reflect the trust our nation place in us.”
Wilson took command of a post where a roughly half of America’s Soldiers are forged.
“You cannot help but be inspired by what Fort Jackson represents to our nation,” Davis added. “Fifty percent of all Soldiers, active, Reserve and National Guard, who enter the U.S. Army begin their journey right here at Fort Jackson. Think about that for a second – half of our entire fighting force is forged on this ground.”
“This is where civilian volunteers who raised their right hand to transform into disciplined, tough American war fighters,” he added. “Fort Jackson is building Soldiers who are prepared, adaptable, and ready for anything our nation calls on them to do, whether that is deterring conflict, deploying overseas, or answering the call in times of crisis.
“That standard is carried out every single day by absolute best of the best: our drill sergeants, instructors, cadre and Department of the Army Civilians.”
Wilson said he was committed to the mission and will lead with purpose.
“My commitment to all of you is to lead with purpose, listen with humility, make decisions with integrity, and keep us focused on readiness, people, and excellence,” he said.
Fort Jackson’s 55th commanding general has deployed multiple times and was previously the deputy commanding general for the Combined Arms Center-Training at Fort Leavenworth, Kansas.
title: Fort Jackson welcomes Wilson as 55th commanding general

Agency recognized for continued investment in veteran hiring and support
WASHINGTON — As Veterans Day approaches, U.S. Customs and Border Protection recognizes the more than 18,000 people who continue serving the nation as part of approximately one-quarter of the agency’s workforce. We would also like to market the release to the surrounding military bases once approved.
Veterans serve throughout the agency as U.S. Border Patrol agents, CBP officers, Air and Marine agents, criminal investigators, mission-support professionals and agency leaders. In fiscal year 2026, CBP hired 1,539 veterans, representing 18.5 percent of all new hires, and will participate in multiple Veteran career fairs throughout the country.
“CBP is proud to recognize the veterans across our workforce whose service to our nation did not end when they left the military,” said CBP Commissioner Rodney S. Scott. “Their professionalism, teamwork, and sense of duty strengthen our mission every day. This Veterans Day, we thank all veterans for their service and their continued contributions to our country.”
Each year, CBP is recognized as a leading employer for veterans. This year, U.S. Veterans Magazine recognized CBP for its commitment to recruiting, hiring and supporting veterans and transitioning service members. The Department of War also recognized CBP for fostering supportive work environments for Reserve and National Guard service members.
CBP’s commitment extends beyond recruitment. Through the CBP Veteran Support Program, employees and their families receive assistance navigating employment benefits, connecting with Department of Veterans Affairs resources, and accessing mental, physical and emotional health support. A worldwide network of approximately 300 coordinators helped 1,151 employees obtain an estimated $18 million in direct compensation during fiscal year 2024.
CBP also supports transitioning service members through the Department of War SkillBridge Internship Program, which provides practical, pre-separation work experience in non-law-enforcement career fields. The agency offers 167 internship opportunities across 25 states, the District of Columbia and Puerto Rico. In fiscal year 2026, CBP hosted 54 SkillBridge interns, 13 of whom were subsequently hired into permanent CBP positions.

Memphis, TN – Two aliens have been indicted in the Western District of Tennessee and are facing federal charges for illegally voting in federal elections. D. Michael Dunavant, United States Attorney for the Western District of Tennessee, announced the unsealing of the indictments today.

As alleged in the indictments, two aliens have been charged for illegally voting in federal elections in the Western District of Tennessee:

Cesar Sanchez Correa, 44, a citizen of Mexico , allegedly illegally voted in Haywood County, TN in the 2024 election held in part for the purpose of electing a candidate for President, Vice President, Member of the United States Senate, or Member of the United States House of Representatives, and allegedly falsely and willfully represented himself to be a citizen of the United States in a Tennessee voter registration application in order to vote in a federal, state, or local election. Sanchez Correa is charged with one count of unlawful voting by an alien, in violation of 18 U.S.C. § 611.

Andreas Van Der Werf, 62, a citizen of Germany , allegedly illegally voted in Fayette County, TN in both the 2022 and 2024 elections held in part for the purpose of electing a candidate for President, Vice President, Member of the United States Senate, or Member of the United States House of Representatives, and allegedly falsely and willfully represented himself to be a citizen of the United States in a Tennessee voter registration application in order to vote in a federal, state, or local election. Van Der Werf is charged with two counts of unlawful voting by an alien, in violation of 18 U.S.C. § 611.

U.S. Attorney D. Michael Dunavant said, “The law is clear: Only American citizens may vote in American elections. Every American citizen must be able to have their vote counted without it being stolen because of fraudulent or ineligible voters. Illegal voting is a crime and will be aggressively prosecuted by the Department of Justice to protect the integrity of the election process.”

“Protecting the integrity of our elections is a responsibility HSI takes seriously,” said HSI Nashville Special Agent in Charge Dennis M. Fetting. “With our partners, we will continue to investigate alleged violations of federal election laws and support efforts to uphold the foundations of our democracy.”

These cases were investigated by the Federal Bureau of Investigation and Homeland Security Investigations, with the assistance of the Tennessee Secretary of State’s Office.

Assistant United States Attorneys from the U.S. Attorney's Office Special Prosecutions Unit will be prosecuting the cases on behalf of the United States.

The charges and allegations contained in the indictment are merely accusations of criminal conduct, not evidence. The defendants are presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt and convicted through due process of law.

###

title: Two Aliens in West Tennessee Charged with Illegal Voting in Federal Elections

NORFOLK, Va. – A Chesapeake woman pled guilty to wire fraud in relation to falsely representing her credentials to provide hair and tattoo removal by laser.

According to court documents, Hayley Nicole Atwood, 33, was licensed by the Virginia Department of Professional and Occupational Regulation as a basic esthetician. Beginning in at least 2017, Atwood consistently falsely purported to be a master esthetician to colleagues and potential customers. Under Virginia law, master estheticians may perform more advanced procedures such as laser hair removal or laser tattoo removal, but only if properly trained and supervised by a licensed physician or physician assistant.

Atwood owned and operated esthetics spas in Chesapeake, Virginia, and Elizabeth City, North Carolina. In March and April of 2021, Atwood purchased two Spectrum Laser devices for her spas. Atwood employed a medical director from December 2019 through July 2021 and a second medical director from July 2021 through November 2022. Neither medical director ever supervised or authorized Atwood or anyone at her business to perform laser tattoo removal. The second director supervised laser hair removal but never evaluated Atwood or her staff or saw her patients. Atwood consistently advertised, offered, and performed laser tattoo and hair removal. Several of Atwood’s clients suffered injury as a result of her laser treatments, including burning and scarring.

Atwood is scheduled to be sentenced on March 5, 2027, and faces up to 20 years in prison. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.

Theophani K. Stamos, First Assistant U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of Virginia; Marie Maguire, Special Agent in Charge, FDA Office of Criminal Investigations, Metro Washington Field Office; and Col. Jeffrey S. Katz, Superintendent of Virginia State Police, made the announcement after U.S. Magistrate Judge Douglas E. Miller accepted the plea.

Assistant U.S. Attorneys Kristen S. Taylor and Rebecca Gantt are prosecuting the case.

Related court documents and information are located on the website of the District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia or on PACER by searching for Case No. 2:26-cr-83.
title: Chesapeake esthetician pleads guilty in laser treatment case

Homeland Security Task Force Investigation Yields Federal Charges for 13 Aliens Charged with Fraud Against the United States
ORLANDO, Fla. — Thirteen aliens from Brazil and Cuba have been charged by indictment for their roles in a conspiracy to defraud the United States and other aliens. The charges include conspiracy to commit wire fraud, wire fraud, visa fraud, unlawful employment of aliens, and marriage fraud. United States Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe made the announcement. U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services provided valuable support to the investigation.
Vagner Sorares De Almeida, 54; Juliana Colucci, 47; Lucas Felipe Trindade Silva, 34; and Ronaldo De Campos, 35, are each charged with one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud and two counts of wire fraud. They are also charged with four counts of conspiracy to commit visa fraud, one count of conspiracy to commit marriage fraud, and one count of unlawful employment of aliens.
Erick Bruno Goncalves De Assis Pinto, 34; Nathalia Da Costa Ferreira, 43; Nathalia Gomes Ciriaco, 29; and Kelen Cristina Da Silva, 37, are each charged with charged with one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud, two counts of wire fraud, and four counts of conspiracy to commit visa fraud.
Issac Antonio Narvaez, 69, is charged with three counts of conspiracy to commit marriage fraud.
Ronay Castillo Salazar, 51; Rebeca Aldama Garcia, 40; Mijail Cabera Nunez, 52; and Lorraine Soares Oliverira, 32, are each charged with one count of conspiracy to commit marriage fraud.
According to court records, from Aug. 18, 2023, through April 20, 2026, Vagner Sorares De Almeida owned and operated a corporate entity registered in Florida called Legacy Imigra Solutions LLC (“Legacy”). Juliana Colucci, Lucas Felipe Trindade Silva, Nathalia Da Costa Ferreira, Nathalia Gomes Ciriaco, Ronaldo De Campos, Erick Bruno Goncalves De Assis Pinto, and Kelen Cristina Da Silva were employees of the company. Legacy falsely purported to be a professional establishment employed by immigration experts and attorneys who could assist individuals with immigration-related legal work. It was part of the conspiracy to give false, inaccurate, and incomplete legal and immigration advice to prospective clients to induce them to retain Legacy’s services. Legacy would falsify immigration documents to fraudulently obtain immigration status and benefits for their clients.
The defendants also engaged in a regular practice of hiring aliens knowing that the individuals were unauthorized for employment in the United States. Vagner Sorares De Almeida, Juliana Colucci, Ronay Castillo Salazar, Rebeca Aldama Garcia, Mijail Cabera Nunez, Lorraine Soares Oliverira, and Issac Antonio Narvaez also conspired to commit marriage fraud.
If convicted, each count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud and wire fraud carries a maximum penalty of 20 years’ imprisonment. The conspiracy to commit visa fraud offenses are each punishable up to 10 years’ imprisonment. The maximum penalty for conspiracy to commit marriage fraud is 5 years in federal prison, and unlawful employment of aliens carries a maximum penalty of 6 months’ imprisonment.
An indictment is merely a formal charge that a defendant has committed one or more violations of federal criminal law, and every defendant is presumed innocent unless, and until, proven guilty.
This case is being investigated by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement’s Homeland Security Investigations (Orlando, Tampa, and Brasilia) and Enforcement and Removal Operations, IRS Criminal Investigation, the Department of Labor Office of Inspector General, the Department of Agriculture Office of Inspector General, USCIS, U.S. Customs and Border Protection, the U.S. Marshals Service, the Orange County Sheriff’s Office, Florida Highway Patrol, and the Florida Department of Law Enforcement. It is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Bianca Bansal.

Nine Charged as a Result of Homeland Security Task Force Investigation into Southeastern Connecticut Cocaine Trafficking
BRIDGEPORT, Conn. - David X. Sullivan, United States Attorney for the District of Connecticut, Jarod Forget, Special Agent in Charge of the Drug Enforcement Administration for New England, and Thomas A. Greco, Special Agent in Charge, ATF Boston Field Division, today announced that the following nine individuals have been charged by indictment with offenses related to the distribution of cocaine and crack cocaine in southeastern Connecticut:
MICHAEL SMITH, also known as “Miz,” 53, of Lisbon
ANTHONY GOMEZ, also known as “Jungle,” 46, of Norwich
ROBERT DURAN, 46, of Mount Vernon, New York
DEONNA WHITE, 48, of Norwich
ROCKY LAURENT, 48, of New London
SARAH BUTLER, 43, of Norwich
HEATHER ROY, 44, of Canterbury
CORDELIA HARRIS, 49, of New London
KEITH NIVAL, 46, of New London
As alleged in court documents and statements made in court, a Homeland Security Task Force investigation, which has included court-authorized wiretaps, video surveillance, GPS tracking of vehicles, and numerous controlled purchases of narcotics, revealed that Smith supplied cocaine and crack to a network of redistributors in southeastern Connecticut. Laurent, Butler, Roy, Harris, and Nival purchased cocaine and crack from Smith and sold it in smaller quantities to their own customers.
It is further alleged that on October 8, 2026, investigators conducting surveillance at a parking lot in Clinton observed Smith, White, and Duran arrive in separate vehicles. Smith retrieved a reusable shopping bag from White’s vehicle and then drove to another area of the lot to meet Duran. Smith gave the bag to Duran who then placed a box in the back of Smith’s vehicle. Smith, White, and Duran were arrested after a search of the box revealed approximately 10 kilograms of cocaine, and a search of the shopping bag revealed more than $170,000 in cash. Butler was also arrested on October 8, after a search of her residence in the Taftville section of Norwich revealed narcotics and drug packaging materials. Investigators also searched two of Smith’s vehicles and found cocaine and crack cocaine packaged for redistribution in one vehicle, and a firearm and more than 200 rounds of ammunition in the other vehicle.
Gomez, Roy, Harris, and Nival were arrested on October 15, 2026, and Laurent has been in state custody since September 23, 2026. Smith, Gomez, Duran, and Nival have been detained since their arrests.
On October 27, 2026, a grand jury in New Haven returned a superseding indictment charging each of the defendants with conspiracy to distribute and to possess with intent to distribute cocaine. If convicted of this charge, based on the quantity of cocaine attributed to each defendant, Smith, Gomez, Duran, White, and Laurent face a mandatory minimum term of imprisonment of 10 years and a maximum term of imprisonment of life; Butler, Harris, and Roy face a mandatory minimum term of imprisonment of five years and a maximum term of imprisonment of 40 years; and Nival faces a maximum term of imprisonment of 20 years.
The indictment also charges Gomez with three counts of possession with intent to distribute, and distribution of, 28 grams or more of cocaine base (“crack”), an offense that carries a mandatory minimum term of imprisonment of five years and a maximum term of imprisonment of 40 years on each count; Smith and Duran with possession with intent to distribute five kilograms or more of cocaine, an offense that carries a mandatory minimum term of imprisonment of 10 years and a maximum term of imprisonment of life; and Smith with unlawful possession of ammunition by a felon, an offense that carries a maximum term of imprisonment of 15 years.
The indictment also seeks the forfeiture of $196,353 in cash and five vehicles seized during the investigation.
U.S. Attorney Sullivan stressed that an indictment is not evidence of guilt. Charges are only allegations, and each defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt.
This matter is being investigated by the Drug Enforcement Administration and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives, with assistance from the Connecticut State Police. The case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Christopher Lembo, Justyn Stokely, and Natasha Freismuth.
This prosecution is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement toward identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States.
HSTF New Haven comprises agents and officers from the FBI, DEA, HSI, ATF, U.S. Postal Inspection Service, Internal Revenue Service – Criminal Investigation, U.S. Department of Transportation – Office of Inspector General, U.S. Department of Labor – Office of Inspector General, U.S. Department of Commerce – Bureau of Industry and Security’s Office of Export Enforcement, and Connecticut State Police, with prosecutions led by the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Connecticut.
title: Nine Charged as a Result of Homeland Security Task Force Investigation into Southeastern Connecticut Cocaine Trafficking
