Fertility medicine discounts through TrumpRx: Launched in February 2026, TrumpRx.gov provides patients with access to discounts (most-favored-nation (MFN) price) on prescription medications, including drugs for infertility and reproductive health conditions that uniquely impact women. There are a range of medical treatments that exist to address ovulatory dysfunction, hormonal imbalances, insulin resistance, or excess weight may improve fertility outcomes.
The Trump Administration is also confronting the high cost of prescription drugs. Through Most-Favored-Nation pricing agreements with 17 major pharmaceutical manufacturers, we have secured substantial relief on many of the country's most widely used medicines. With the launch of TrumpRx.gov, patients now have direct access to lower drug prices in line with those paid by other developed nations. We remain committed to increasing price transparency and ending surprise billing so that families are never caught off guard by unexpected costs.
From the WH Fact Sheet: Massive savings on some of the most commonly used fertility medications in the country to help families grow. Many patients struggling with infertility pay for their medicines out-of-pocket, meaning they will stand to save more than $2,000 per cycle of fertility drugs, on average.
- Gonal-F, one of the most commonly used fertility drugs, will see its price reduced to as low as $168 per pen, depending on dosage strength.
- The price of Cetrotide, another commonly used fertility medicine, will drop from $316 to $22.50.
- The price of Ovidrel will fall from $251 to $84.

WASHINGTON — The United States and Mexico announced today a memorandum of understanding regarding denial of rights concerns at the Industrias Tecnos, S.A. de C.V. (Industrias Tecnos or the company) facility located in Cuernavaca, Morelos, Mexico, where the company manufactures small arms ammunition.
The memorandum of understanding details a plan to remedy violations of Mexican law at the facility and includes actions aimed at ensuring freedom of association and collective bargaining rights are protected at the facility moving forward.
Under the terms of the memorandum of understanding, the Government of Mexico (Mexico) will ensure that Industrias Tecnos takes various remedial actions, including to:
- Verify proper compensation for dismissed workers as required by Mexican law, for any wages or benefits those workers did not receive as a result of unlawful dismissals;
- Implement and train all company personnel on a neutrality statement and guidelines related to the freedom of association and collective bargaining, including a zero-tolerance policy for violations, and commit to additional retraining as needed;
- Install and publicize a complaint mechanism through which workers can report violations of their rights and breaches of company policies anonymously and confidentially; and
- Maintain on the company website and in any internal communications platform the neutrality statement and guidelines, training materials, and information about complaint mechanisms maintained by the company and Mexico, such that the information is easily accessible to workers.
Under the terms of the memorandum of understanding, Mexico will, among other actions:
- Review and verify determinations made in relation to dismissed workers identified by the United States to ensure outcomes were effectuated in accordance with Mexican law;
- Monitor the facility with regard to the obligations of the memorandum of understanding and compliance with Mexican laws related to freedom of association and collective bargaining;
- Conduct in-person training that is structured to ensure all workers understand their right to freedom of association and collective bargaining and how to exercise it;
- Conduct separate workers’ rights training for supervisors, human resources and labor relations personnel, and other high-level and “trusted” officials; and
- Maintain a direct email address, reporting platform, and telephone line for workers to anonymously report any potential acts of unlawful interference or other violations of freedom of association and collective bargaining rights, and timely investigate any allegations.
The United States and Mexico agreed to establish a deadline of October 15, 2026, to complete the actions listed in the memorandum of understanding.
Background
The United States Trade Representative and the Secretary of Labor co-chair the Interagency Labor Committee for Monitoring and Enforcement (ILC). On May 23, 2024, the ILC received a Rapid Response Labor Mechanism (RRM) petition from Sindicato Independiente de Trabajadores y Empleados, Transporte, Carga y Descarga, Exploración y Explotación de Minerales Básicos, Productos Metálicos, Similares y Conexos de la República Mexicana (Sindicato Metálico), a Mexican labor union. The petition alleged an ongoing Denial of Rights by Industrias Tecnos at its facility in Morelos, Mexico. The ILC reviews RRM petitions that it receives, and the accompanying information, within 30 days. The ILC determined that there was sufficient, credible evidence of a denial of rights enabling the good faith invocation of enforcement mechanisms.
As a result, on June 24, 2024, the United States submitted a request that Mexico review the matter, and Mexico thereafter agreed to conduct a review. After Mexico issued a report finding no Denial of Rights at the facility, the United States requested the establishment of a panel pursuant to Article 31-A.5.1(a) of the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement.
Read the full memorandum of understanding here.
Read an unofficial courtesy Spanish translation of the full memorandum of understanding here.
###
title: United States and Mexico Announce Memorandum of Understanding at Industrias Tecnos Facility

Oregon Delegation Celebrates Federal Support for Oregon’s Hazelnut, Seafood Industries
Washington, D.C. – Today, Oregon’s U.S. Senator Jeff Merkley led Oregon Congressional Delegation members—including Senator Ron Wyden and U.S. Representatives Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01), Val Hoyle (OR-04), Andrea Salinas (OR-06), Maxine Dexter (OR-03), and Janelle Bynum (OR-05)—to announce that after pressure from the delegation, the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) will purchase hazelnuts and Pacific Whiting fillets under the agency’s Section 32 purchase program. These purchases will benefit communities and rural economies across Oregon by supporting domestic production and distribution of these agricultural goods during periods of significant market disruption and economic uncertainty.
“Our fisheries and farms deliver incredible products all around the world and are the lifeblood of our communities,” said Merkley, who led the Oregon delegation in pressing USDA to include hazelnuts and whiting in its latest food purchase. “This announcement ensures Oregon’s harvesters, processors, and producers will receive critical financial assistance needed to continue operating and providing services here in Oregon and beyond. I am elated the USDA has decided to make these purchases—this is a win for communities across our state.”
“Iconic state industries like agriculture and fishing count on the U.S. Department of Agriculture to do its job and support Oregonians working hard to keep producing their world-class goods,” said Wyden. “I’m glad the full-court press from the delegation has unlocked this win for Oregonians fishing Pacific whiting and growing hazelnuts.”
“Oregonians know that hazelnuts and seafood are some of the state’s most popular and delicious products,” said Bonamici. “Our growers and producers work tirelessly and bolster the local economy. I’m glad the USDA is making this investment.”
“These investments from the USDA will support the people who harvest, process and bring Pacific Whiting fish and hazelnuts to market,” said Hoyle. “By putting Oregon fishermen and farmers first, we’re boosting our coastal and rural economies."
“Oregon’s specialty crop growers are the backbone of our economy, but too many are struggling with rising costs and uncertain markets,” said Salinas. “In the Willamette Valley, generations of farmers have depended on the hazelnut industry for their livelihoods. That’s why I joined my colleagues in pushing USDA to purchase Oregon hazelnuts and Pacific whiting. These purchases will provide much-needed support for our growers and fishing communities while putting more Oregon-grown and Oregon-caught food onto kitchen tables. I’m proud we secured this win for Oregon producers, and I’ll keep fighting to make sure our specialty crop farmers have the markets and resources they need to succeed.”
"Oregon’s farmers and fishermen work hard to feed our communities, and they deserve a federal government that stands behind them,” said Dexter. “Our delegation pushed USDA to act, and these $34 million in purchases will support Oregon’s hazelnut growers and fishermen during a difficult economic stretch. This investment will help sustain local jobs, strengthen rural and coastal economies, and get nutritious food to families who need it.”
“Our farmers are putting in the work every day to keep Oregon families fed,” said Bynum. “And they’re not just helping put food on the table, they’re keeping money with our families, creating good jobs close to home, and giving people what they need to put down roots here in Oregon. Money back in our state and with our farmers is a win-win.”
Previously, Merkley and the Oregon delegation pressed the USDA to include Pacific whiting and Oregon hazelnuts, which account for 99 percent of hazelnuts produced in the United States, in this year’s Section 32 purchases. Following their efforts, the USDA announced it was purchasing $22 million in hazelnuts and $12 million in Pacific whiting.
###
title: Oregon Delegation Celebrates Federal Support for Oregon’s Hazelnut, Seafood Industries

Congressman Davis Announces $2.6 Million VA Award for Eastern Carolina State Veterans Cemetery Expansion
WASHINGTON, DC – Congressman Don Davis (NC-01) announced that the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs has awarded $2,613,394 to support the expansion of the Eastern Carolina State Veterans Cemetery in Goldsboro.
“Such a historic investment in the Veterans Cemetery Grants Program will help to expand the Eastern Carolina State Veterans Cemetery, allowing more veterans to be laid to rest closer to home,” said Congressman Don Davis.
As a former U.S. Air Force mortuary officer, Congressman Davis remains committed to the support of our veterans, our military families, and the resources and programs available to them. “Our veterans should be able to receive the final honor they so rightfully deserve. They stood for America. We owe them and their families the honor, respect, and dignity they have earned,” Davis added.
The Eastern Carolina State Veterans Cemetery is one of 21 cemeteries across the country that will receive VA cemetery grants in Fiscal Year 2026. The U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs will also reimburse the cost of pre-placed crypts and their delivery to the cemetery up to $2,878.
The Veterans Cemetery Grants Program is used by states, territories, and Native American tribes to establish, expand, improve, and maintain veterans cemeteries across the country. The U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs awarded a record $106.5 million in grants through the program in Fiscal Year 2026.
Congressman Don Davis is a 1994 U.S. Air Force Academy graduate and a U.S. Air Force veteran. He serves as the vice ranking member of the U.S. House Armed Services Committee, where he serves on the Readiness and Tactical Air and Land Forces subcommittees.
###
title: Congressman Davis Announces $2.6 Million VA Award for Eastern Carolina State Veterans Cemetery Expansion

US Department of Labor launches Registered Apprenticeship incentive payments for high-growth industries
WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of Labor announced today that Registered Apprenticeship sponsors can begin applying for direct payments of up to $6,000 per apprentice through the Pay-for-Performance Incentive Payments Program. The opening of applications follows President Trump’s announcement on Friday in Daytona Beach, Florida, of the department’s $40 million investment, led by the Florida Department of Commerce, to expand Registered Apprenticeships in shipbuilding and the defense industrial base, which is projected to lead to nearly 10,000 new apprentices over the next four years. Applications will be accepted on a rolling basis until all available funds have been obligated. To date, the department has invested nearly $200 million in pay-for-performance incentive funds.
In July, the department awarded nearly $162 million to five organizations to lead nationwide training programs for thousands of Americans seeking jobs in priority industry sectors including shipbuilding and the defense industrial base, super intelligence, semiconductor and nuclear energy infrastructure, telecommunications, information technology, and transportation. The funding will help employers hire and retain new apprentices, reduce barriers that limit employer participation, and fill in-demand jobs in these industries.
The Pay-for-Performance Incentive Payments Program builds on the American Manufacturing Apprenticeship Incentive Fund, a $35.8 million cooperative agreement established to expand Registered Apprenticeship programs in advanced manufacturing nationwide.
During a visit to Florida today, U.S. Secretary of Labor Keith Sonderling joined Rep. Brian Mast, Florida Education Commissioner Henry Mack, and Florida Commerce Deputy Secretary of Economic Development Jason Mahon to highlight the opening of applications and the positive impact these grants will have on Florida’s workforce.
“The Trump Administration is committed to rapidly expanding Registered Apprenticeships as a core strategy to fill jobs in high-growth, high-demand industries,” said Secretary Sonderling. “Delivering direct support to employers and other Registered Apprenticeship program sponsors is the fastest way to help skilled Americans enter the workforce while also strengthening our nation’s economy.”
Here’s how each active incentive fund supports training and employment opportunities:
- American Manufacturing Apprenticeship Incentive Fund – The Arkansas Department of Commerce, Division of Workforce Services, administers this $35.8 million fund to support Registered Apprenticeships in advanced manufacturing. Sponsors with eligible occupations may receive up to $3,500 per new apprentice, with funding available for up to 200 apprentices per sponsor. Sponsors are required to provide employers with at least 90% of the total incentive fund payment they receive.
- Information Technology Apprenticeship Incentive Fund – The Trustees of Clark University administer this $27 million fund to support Registered Apprenticeships in information technology occupations. Sponsors with eligible occupations may receive a one-time incentive payment of $6,000 for each eligible new apprentice who remains employed for at least 90 days.
- Shipbuilding and Defense Industrial Base Apprenticeship Incentive Fund – The Florida Department of Commerce administers this $40 million fund to support Registered Apprenticeships in occupations tied to shipbuilding and the defense industrial base. Sponsors with eligible occupations may receive a baseline payment of $2,000 for each new apprentice who remains employed for at least 90 days, with payments of up to $6,000 available to Registered Apprenticeship sponsors that meet at least one strategic priority area.
- Super Intelligence, Semiconductor, and Nuclear Energy Infrastructure Apprenticeship Incentive Fund – Jobs for the Future Inc. administers this $40 million fund, which supports Registered Apprenticeships in super intelligence, data centers, semiconductor fabrication, nuclear energy infrastructure, and quantum-related fields. Sponsors with eligible occupations may receive up to $6,000 per eligible new apprentice, paid in two installments: $3,750 after 90 days of retention, and $2,250 upon program completion or after 12 months, whichever occurs first.
- Telecommunication Apprenticeship Incentive Fund – The Wireless Infrastructure Association administers this $29.9 million fund to support Registered Apprenticeships in telecommunications occupations. Sponsors with eligible occupations may receive up to $6,000 per eligible new apprentice across three milestones: $1,500 after 90 days of retention, $2,500 upon completion of related technical instruction, and $2,000 upon successful completion of the program.
- Transportation Automotive Technician Apprenticeship Incentive Fund – The ASE Education Foundation administers this $25 million fund to support Registered Apprenticeships for automotive and truck service technicians. Sponsors with eligible occupations may receive $3,500 per apprentice, including an initial $2,500 payment at the 90-day retention benchmark and an additional $1,000 payment after nine months.
title: US Department of Labor launches Registered Apprenticeship incentive payments for high-growth industries

BIRMINGHAM, Ala. – In response to multiple acts of violence in and around the Birmingham region over the past several days the U.S. Attorney for the Northern District of Alabama is issuing the following statement:

- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: Through pro-growth policies and tough trade deals, President Trump has fortified the dollar’s dominance, preventing de-dollarization efforts abroad and ensuring it remains the global standard — boosting American economic power worldwide.
- PROMISE MADE: “I will be a champion for the American worker, who has suffered under lopsided trade deals that have pillaged our country. That will end on my watch, and we will use tariffs to fight against unfair trade practices by other countries and foster our own industrial growth.” (11/3/24)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump has delivered better terms for American workers, farmers, and manufacturers by leveling the economic playing field with our trading partners. By using tariffs as leverage, President Trump secured new and improved trade agreements with major U.S. trading partners covering more than half of global GDP — including the United Kingdom, European Union, Japan, China, India, Republic of Korea, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, the Philippines, and Cambodia.
- PROMISE MADE: “We’re going to tariff the hell out of countries that have been taking advantage of us…” (11/3/24)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump has used tariffs as a strategic tool to rebuild American manufacturing, secure our supply chains, and protect U.S. national security. After decades of weak trade policies that allowed foreign nations to exploit our economy, close off certain markets to U.S. exports, and flood American markets with dumped goods, America is finally getting tough on trade and delivering results. When the Supreme Court ruled against his emergency tariffs, President Trump kept the pressure on, turning to Section 122, Section 232, and Section 301 tariffs to keep defending American workers.
- PROMISE MADE: “We’re going to put very serious tariffs on Mexico and Canada because… The drugs that are coming through are at record numbers.” (1/7/25)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump kept his word, leveraging tariffs on Mexico and Canada to stop the flow of fentanyl and its precursor chemicals in their tracks and secure agreements with the two countries to work together to protect national security against these deadly drugs. Fentanyl trafficking at the southern border has collapsed by 56%, and President Trump signed the HALT Fentanyl Act to permanently classify fentanyl analogues as Schedule I drugs. As a result, drug overdose deaths have plunged to the lowest since 2017.
- PROMISE MADE: “[China is] sending fentanyl into our country — and because of that, they’re causing us hundreds of thousands of deaths, so China is going to end up paying a tariff also for that… China has to stop sending fentanyl into our country and killing our people.” (1/30/25)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump utilized tariffs as a powerful tool to force China to commit to working with the U.S. to stop the flow of fentanyl and precursor chemicals — culminating in an historic meeting with President Xi Jinping, where the two leaders pledged cooperation on solving the problem. President Trump also designated illicit fentanyl and its core precursors as Weapons of Mass Destruction.
- PROMISE MADE: “Together, we’re going to… bring thousands of factories back to the USA, right where they belong — and that will be done through tariffs and smart policy. We will build American, we will buy American, and we will hire American.” (1/19/25)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: As President Trump pursues his bold commitment to an America First trade agenda, companies and countries have committed tens of trillions in new investment in the U.S. — positioning the U.S. as the dominant player for the jobs of the future.
- PROMISE MADE: “We are a nation whose once-revered airports are dirty, crowded mess… They don’t seek the qualified air traffic controllers and they just don’t know what the hell they’re doing.” (5/18/24)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump unveiled a plan to modernize America’s woefully outdated air traffic control system to keep travelers safe. With initial funding from the Working Families Tax Cuts, the FAA is replacing outdated radar, radios, software, and telecommunications equipment at more than 4,600 sites nationwide — the first step in building a brand-new air traffic control system for the American people. Meanwhile, the Trump Administration is also investing in modernizing our nation’s airports, including at Washington Dulles International Airport.
Putting America’s Farmers and Ranchers First
- PROMISE MADE: “I will take immediate steps to defeat inflation, increase real farm incomes, and grow the agricultural economy by unleashing American energy, slashing wasteful government spending, and cutting burdensome regulation.” (2024)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump has delivered $12 billion in Farmer Bridge payments to American farmers hurt by unfair foreign trade practices and record input costs left by the Biden Administration, as well as historic farm safety net investments in the Working Families Tax Cuts, raising reference prices for major crops like soybeans, corn, and wheat by 10–21%.
- PROMISE MADE: “To protect the pro-farmer tax cuts I delivered in 2017, including the elimination of the estate tax, or death tax, as well as the giant tax cut I gave to family farms… I will also make permanent the provisions of the Trump Tax Cuts and Jobs Act.” (2024)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: The Working Families Tax Cuts protect  family farms and ranches from the death tax by permanently raising the exemption and indexing it to inflation, so generational farm families aren’t forced to sell land, equipment, or livestock to pay the IRS.
- PROMISE MADE: “When you buy apples, when you buy bacon, when you buy eggs, they would double and triple the price over a short period of time… We’re going to bring those prices way down.” (12/8/24)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: The Trump Administration launched a $1 billion plan to combat bird flu, protect America’s poultry flocks, and lower egg prices — resulting in the average price of a dozen eggs plunging more than 60%.
- PROMISE MADE: “Just as I moved the Bureau of Land Management to Colorado, as many as 100,000 government positions can be moved out. And I mean immediately out of Washington to places filled with patriots who love America.” (3/21/23)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: The Trump Administration announced a sweeping reorganization of the Department of Agriculture, moving more than half of the D.C.-area workforce out of the swamp to locations nationwide — bringing the Department closer to the farmers and ranchers it serves.
- PROMISE MADE: “I will once again stand up for Iowa ethanol…” (12/19/23)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: In 2025, the Trump Administration cleared summer sales of E15 nationwide, waived all federal barriers to E10, and implemented the highest-ever renewable fuel volume requirements.
Unleashing American Energy Dominance
- PROMISE MADE: “We will stop the Biden-Harris war on American energy … American energy is such a big deal. We will drill, baby, drill.” (8/3/24)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump has unleashed American energy independence like never before, approving more drilling permits on federal lands than in any year in the past 15 years, lifting burdensome regulations, exporting to foreign countries, opening millions of acres for mining and drilling, terminating Biden-era preferential treatment for unreliable, foreign-controlled wind energy, and expanding pipelines — and as a result, U.S. oil and natural gas production surged to record levels in 2025 and is on track for another record in 2026.
- PROMISE MADE: “I will immediately issue a national emergency declaration to achieve massive increase in domestic energy supply…” (9/5/24)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: On Day One, President Trump declared a national energy emergency to eliminate bureaucratic barriers, unleash innovation, and restore America’s position as the world’s leading energy producer.
- PROMISE MADE: “I will sign Day One orders to… cancel [Biden’s] natural gas export ban.” (12/22/24)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump took executive action to lift the Biden-era freeze on gas exports and secured a $54 billion deal with Korea and Taiwan to build the long-stalled natural gas pipeline in Alaska.
- PROMISE MADE: “[Biden] canceled the Keystone pipeline — 48,000 jobs and something that would have been fantastic for energy… It was a very important pipeline, actually, but we’ll get it open.” (9/7/24)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: In April 2026, President Trump signed a cross-border permit for a pipeline project that would revive large parts of the Keystone XL using idle Keystone XL pipe to carry Canadian oil to Wyoming.
- PROMISE MADE: “We’re going to be opening up ANWR.” (1/7/25)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump freed up millions of acres within ANWR for oil and gas drilling and mining.
- PROMISE MADE: “Banning offshore drilling will not stand. I will reverse it immediately.” (1/7/25)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump revoked Biden-era orders prohibiting offshore oil and gas leasing almost immediately after taking office and the Working Families Tax Cuts Act mandated a minimum of 30 offshore lease sales in the Gulf of America through 2040.
- PROMISE MADE: “I told the European Union that they must make up their tremendous deficit with the United States by the large-scale purchase of our oil and gas. Otherwise, it is TARIFFS all the way!!!” (12/20/24)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump secured a historic commitment from the European Union to purchase $750 billion of American energy — and after the capture of Maduro, President Trump’s unprecedented Venezuela oil deal delivered its first million barrels to Texas in October 2026 at zero cost to taxpayers.
- PROMISE MADE: “We have the minerals, but we don’t have the environmental impact statements — but we’ll make sure that that’s going to go very quickly. We’ll be able to do things that you never even thought.” (9/27/24)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump signed an Executive Order to fast-track mining permits and unlock domestic production of critical minerals. The Trump Administration also struck a key partnership with MP Materials to build America’s rare earth magnet supply chain and finally end American dependence on China.
Ending the Green New Scam
- PROMISE MADE: “I will… end the Green New Scam.” (10/24/24)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump immediately targeted the costly Green New Scam through executive action, freezing funding to Radical Left climate programming that had zero accountability to taxpayers and drove energy costs up, while the Working Families Tax Cuts further repealed Green New Scam policies. The Trump Administration has also weeded out nonsense “climate” initiatives across the federal government.
- PROMISE MADE: “We’re going to be ending the electric car mandate quickly.” (1/7/25)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump revoked the Biden-era electric vehicle mandate and fortified that action by signing three congressional resolutions into law ending California’s EV mandate and emission standards.
- PROMISE MADE: “I’m immediately withdrawing from the unfair, one-sided Paris Climate Accord rip-off. The United States will not sabotage our own industries while China pollutes with impunity.” (1/20/25)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: On Day One, President Trump withdrew the U.S. from the Paris Climate Accord — and in January 2026, he pulled America out of 66 international organizations that promote radical climate policies and globalist ideologies. In February 2026, the Trump Administration eliminated the Obama-era 2009 Endangerment Finding in the single largest deregulatory action in U.S. history, saving American taxpayers over $1.3 trillion.
- PROMISE MADE: “We are going to make sure that [offshore wind] ends on Day One. I’m going to write it out in an Executive Order.” (5/11/24)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: On Day One, President Trump withdrew every area of the Outer Continental Shelf from new offshore wind leasing and ordered a full review of the federal government’s wind leasing and permitting practices.
- PROMISE MADE: “I will end all of these ridiculous quality of life-destroying mandates, just as I did just three-and-a-half years ago.” (5/1/24)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump scrapped the Biden-era showerhead water pressure rule, which unnecessarily restricted water pressure for Americans, and axed costly appliance efficiency mandates that drove up prices for American families.
Protecting America’s Land, Air, and Water
- PROMISE MADE: “I want clean, beautiful air and clean, beautiful water. That’s all crystal clean water, and we want clean air.” (10/1/24)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump established the Make America Beautiful Again Commission to conserve America’s national parks, forests, waterways, and public lands, restore routine maintenance after years of neglect, and expand access for hunters, fishers, hikers, and outdoorsmen.
- PROMISE MADE: “We want to get that water pouring down here as quickly as possible and let hundreds of millions of gallons of water flow down into Southern California.” (1/24/25)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump directed federal agencies to restart his first-term plan to route more water from the Sacramento–San Joaquin Delta to the Central Valley and Southern California, where farms and families desperately need a reliable water supply.
Slashing Red Tape and Draining the Swamp
- PROMISE MADE: “To reduce costs for both manufacturers and consumers, I will remove ten old regulations for every new regulation.” (10/10/24)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: Last year, President Trump finalized an unprecedented 646 deregulatory actions compared to just five significant regulatory actions for a ratio of 129-to-1 — nearly 13 times the President’s 10-to-1 target — saving Americans an estimated $211.8 billion.
- PROMISE MADE: “I will be signing an Executive Order next week ending the ridiculous Biden push for Paper Straws, which don’t work. BACK TO PLASTIC!” (2/7/25)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: Three days later, President Trump signed an Executive Order ending the federal procurement and forced use of paper straws.
- PROMISE MADE: “We’re going to go back to a merit system.” (8/29/24)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: The Trump Administration rolled out new merit-based federal hiring plans — ensuring the government’s hiring decisions are based on merit only.
- PROMISE MADE: “We’re going to clean out the corrupt, broken, and failing bureaucracies.” (11/14/24)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: The Trump Administration has dramatically downsized the scope of the federal bureaucracy, driving federal employment to 2.68 million — the lowest level since 1966 — finally ensuring government is serving the taxpayers who fund it.
- PROMISE MADE: “I will immediately re-issue my 2020 Executive Order restoring the President’s authority to remove rogue bureaucrats, and I will wield that power very aggressively.” (3/21/23)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: On Day One, President Trump restored accountability for policy-influencing positions in the federal workforce. The Office of Personnel Management then finalized a rule so employees in these positions can be held accountable for poor performance or misconduct.
- PROMISE MADE: “If people don’t come back to work, come back into the office, they’re going to be dismissed.” (12/16/24)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: On Day One, President Trump ordered every federal department and agency to end remote work arrangements and require employees to return to work in person, full time.
- PROMISE MADE: “We’re going to stop the destructive and divisive diversity, equity, and inclusion mandates…” (1/19/25)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: The Trump Administration immediately ended the radical and wasteful government-sponsored DEI programming and preferencing that hindered the federal bureaucracy from effectively serving the taxpayers — and has rolled back woke DEI programming across higher education and corporate America.
- PROMISE MADE: “My Administration will establish the brand-new Department of Government Efficiency.” (1/20/25)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: On Day One, President Trump established the Department of Government Efficiency; the Trump Administration’s government efficiency initiatives have saved taxpayers an estimated $215 billion.
- PROMISE MADE: “NO MORE FUNDING FOR NPR, A TOTAL SCAM! … THEY ARE A LIBERAL DISINFORMATION MACHINE. NOT ONE DOLLAR!!!” (4/10/24)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump ordered an end to the taxpayer subsidization of biased media at NPR and PBS, then signed the Rescissions Act of 2025 into law — clawing back more than $1 billion from the Corporation for Public Broadcasting, the taxpayer-funded backer of PBS and NPR. In January 2026, CPB’s board voted to dissolve the Corporation.
Restoring Peace Through Strength
- PROMISE MADE: “I’ll insist that every NATO nation must spend at least 3%.” (8/26/24)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump secured an agreement from NATO member nations to raise their defense spending to 5% of their GDP by 2035 — a remarkable foreign policy feat long thought impossible. European allies and Canada increased their defense spending by nearly 20% in 2025 alone.
- PROMISE MADE: “We gave it to Panama, and we’re taking it back.” (1/20/25)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: Since President Trump took office, Panama has pulled out of China’s Belt and Road Initiative, and in January 2026, Panama’s Supreme Court annulled the contracts that let a Hong Kong-based company run two ports on the canal.
- PROMISE MADE: “We will expel the warmongering from our government.” (8/9/23)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump has achieved remarkable success, leveraging his dealmaking ability to achieve unprecedented peace in eight conflicts throughout the world — including between India and Pakistan, Israel and Iran, the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda, Cambodia and Thailand, Kosovo and Serbia, Egypt and Ethiopia, Armenia and Azerbaijan, and Israel and Hamas — and he is now driving the push for trilateral talks to end the war between Russia and Ukraine.
- PROMISE MADE: “…if the hostages are not released prior to January 20, 2025, the date that I proudly assume Office as President of the United States, there will be ALL HELL TO PAY in the Middle East…” (12/2/24)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump’s Gaza Peace Plan brought every remaining hostage home and established a Board of Peace for regional security. President Trump has also secured the release of scores of detained Americans abroad, including hostages from Venezuela, Afghanistan, Russia, and Belarus.
- PROMISE MADE: “For purposes of National Security and Freedom throughout the World, the United States of America feels that the ownership and control of Greenland is an absolute necessity.” (12/22/24)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump achieved a major agreement with Denmark and Greenland that gives America permanent basing rights, access to new U.S. defense areas, and bars any adversary from establishing a military presence there without America’s approval, all at no cost to American taxpayers.
- PROMISE MADE: “She supported removing the Houthis [from] a list. We had a terror list that was really very important for them to be on that terror list.” (9/5/24); “Look at what’s happening with the Houthis… I will get that settled.” (9/10/24)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump ordered the Iran-backed Houthis re-designated as a Foreign Terrorist Organization, reversing Biden’s reckless delisting, and the State Department finalized the designation weeks later. The Trump Administration also designated the Egyptian, Jordanian, and Lebanese branches of the Muslim Brotherhood as terrorist organizations for their ties to Iran and support for Hamas.
- PROMISE MADE: “Iran can’t have a nuclear weapon. Nuclear weapons are the greatest single threat to our country, but to the entire world.” (11/3/24)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: In Operation Midnight Hammer, U.S. forces obliterated the Iranian regime’s key nuclear facilities at Fordow, Natanz, and Esfahan. Then, in Operation Epic Fury, U.S. forces achieved every military objective in just 38 days of major combat — destroying more than 85% of Iran’s defense industrial base and 150 Iranian warships, including every submarine — as President Trump’s naval blockade costs the regime at least $25 billion in oil revenue. As President Trump has made clear, Iran will NEVER have a nuclear weapon.
- PROMISE MADE: “Any country that does business with Iran is not going to do any business with the United States.” (12/2/23)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump enacted crippling sanctions on the Iranian regime — and Operation Economic Outcast targeted the regime’s international financial networks and shadow banking networks that enabled their funding of terrorism around the world and nuclear ambitions.
- PROMISE MADE: “Iran was broke under Donald Trump. Now Iran has $300 billion because they took off all the sanctions that I had.” (9/10/24)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump immediately restored maximum pressure on the Iranian regime, ordering his Administration to drive Iran’s oil exports to zero. Then, with the Trump Administration’s backing, United Nations sanctions on Iran snapped back into place.
Putting America First on the World Stage
- PROMISE MADE: “The departments and agencies that have been weaponized will be completely overhauled so that faceless bureaucrats will never again be able to target and persecute conservatives.” (3/21/23)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: The Trump Administration launched a comprehensive reorganization of the State Department, eliminating costly redundancies, ending programs that do not serve America’s national interests, and reducing the bloated bureaucracy. The Trump Administration also defunded USAID, ending decades of waste, fraud, and taxpayer-funded globalist projects designed to serve the Deep State, not the American people.
- PROMISE MADE: “We will drive out the globalists.” (7/18/24)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump immediately rejected the globalist agreements that surrendered American sovereignty to Deep State actors and foreign bureaucrats. On Day One, President Trump declared that Biden’s global minimum tax deal has no force or effect in the United States, then secured a G7 agreement shielding American companies from its key provisions. The Trump Administration also rejected the World Health Organization’s power grab.
Rebuilding the Strongest Military the World Has Ever Seen
- PROMISE MADE: “We will again build the strongest military the world has ever seen.” (1/20/25)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: With the largest military investment in decades — including more than $156 billion in new defense funding signed into law — President Trump is modernizing our forces with cutting-edge technology, rebuilding depleted stockpiles, and ensuring our troops are the best-equipped in history — deterring adversaries and keeping America safe. At the same time, military recruitment is surging as the Armed Forces return to their warfighting standards of excellence: the Navy, Marine Corps, Air Force, and Space Force all met or exceeded their FY 2026 recruiting goals.
- PROMISE MADE: “We will build a great Iron Dome over our country… a state-of-the-art missile defense shield that will be entirely built in America and create jobs, jobs, jobs.” (6/15/24)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump announced a draft architecture and implementation plan for a Golden Dome missile defense system to protect our homeland from 21st Century threats — and secured $24.4 billion for it in the Working Families Tax Cuts. The program has already obligated about 90% of the funds it has received and has radars, interceptors, and space-based interceptors on contract.
- PROMISE MADE: “This New American Industrialism will create millions and millions of jobs… We will be able to build ships again.” (9/24/24)
- ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump signed an Executive Order to restore America’s maritime dominance, established a new Office of Maritime and Industrial Capacity at the National Security Council in the White House to prioritize growi
title: President Trump’s Second Term: Promises Made, Promises Kept, Results Delivered

text:
Introduction
The economy under the Trump Administration is strong, supported by robust business investment in equipment and intellectual property products, as well as solid household consumption growth. Business fixed investment (BFI) rose by over 10% at an annual rate over the first three quarters of 2026, driven by investments in new equipment and intellectual property. Since December 2025, the private sector has added 634,000 net new jobs across a broadening range of industries. The unemployment rate and initial unemployment claims remain low, and real weekly wages have grown since the President’s inauguration.
Real Gross Domestic Product (GDP)
The economy in the third quarter of 2026 (3Q26) grew at the fastest pace in the last four quarters. According to the advance estimate, real GDP grew by 3.4% at an annual rate, accelerating sharply from the 2.2% advance in 2Q26. Core demand in the private sector remained unusually strong, with private domestic final purchases (PDFP) – the combination of PCE, BFI, and residential investment – rising 4.9% at an annual rate, the strongest pace in over five years and following a 4.6% gain in 2Q. Apart from outsized growth of PDFP in the recovery from the short pandemic recession, these were the first back-to-back gains above 4.5% since 2014. The robust PDFP growth in 2Q and 3Q26 suggests a marked boost in the economy’s already-solid capacity for self-sustaining growth in future quarters.
- BFI grew by 12.7% at an annual rate in 3Q26 – after the very rapid paces of 9.0% in 2Q and 9.9% in 1Q26 – and alone contributed 1.8 percentage points to GDP growth. The third quarter’s rate was the fastest in 15 years, outside of wide swings seen during the pandemic.
  - Equipment investment surged by 20.9% at an annual rate, the third consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, bringing the annualized rate thus far in 2026 to 16.6%. While super intelligence-related (SI-related) investments contributed to record levels of equipment capital expenditure through the first three quarters, capital expenditure growth was broad-based in 3Q26. Industrial equipment investment rose at an annual rate of 24.7%, following 27.0% annualized growth in 2Q26.
  - Investment in intellectual property products expanded by 8.4% at an annual rate, reflecting businesses’ continued high levels of investment in software, as well as research and development.
  - Structures investment turned strongly positive in 3Q26, rising 5.4% at an annual rate, after inching up 0.1% in the previous quarter. Structures investment in 3Q26 was the strongest since 4Q23, and this quarter marked the first back-to-back quarterly gains in structures investment in three years. Spending on data centers accelerated to a triple-digit pace in 3Q26.
- Persistently strong personal consumption expenditures (PCE), which account for roughly two-thirds of the U.S. economy, remained the largest contributor to GDP growth. PCE grew by 3.8% at an annual rate in 3Q26, matching the 2Q pace and adding 2.5 percentage points to real GDP growth. Consumer spending on services accelerated in 3Q26 (led by both health care services and food services and accommodations), while goods spending remained solid (led by prescription drugs).
- Residential investment declined by 3.3% at an annual rate, reversing a 2.8% increase in 2Q. The decrease in residential investment shaved 0.1 percentage points from growth. Spending on single-family structures and brokers’ commissions (the latter related to existing home sales) both declined, more than offsetting a slight increase in multifamily structures investment.
Of the remaining components of GDP, the trade deficit widened, posing a larger drag on growth. Exports of goods and services declined, led by petroleum and related products—though exports of intellectual property services increased at a double-digit rate. Meanwhile, imports surged, largely due to non-automotive capital goods. These imports are enabling U.S. businesses to meet the increased demand arising from a boom in capital expenditures. On balance, net exports subtracted 3.3 percentage points from GDP growth.
By contrast, the change in private inventories and total government spending both added to economic growth. The federal contribution to growth surged, reflecting more national defense expenditures as well as less drawdown in the Strategic Petroleum Reserve. Meanwhile, state and local government expenditures were essentially flat. Public spending and the change in private inventories added a combined 2.5 percentage points to real GDP growth in 3Q26.
Labor Markets
Job growth remained consistent with breakeven employment in 3Q26, and other measures of labor markets remained healthy (see Table 2 – Labor Market Indicators). Private-sector employment growth and the unemployment rate indicate a full-employment economy—one that has steady job growth with neither rising unemployment nor inflationary pressures from wages. The prime-age (ages 25 to 54) labor force participation rate (LFPR) remained at a high level despite a slight decline in the overall LFPR. Job openings were relatively stable in both absolute terms and relative to the number of unemployed persons. Preliminary 4Q26 readings indicate that unemployment claims through mid-October stand near multi-decade lows.
- Net new payrolls averaged 51,000 per month in 3Q26. Year to date, establishments have added an average of 68,000 jobs per month in 2026.
  - The private sector continues to lead job growth, and payroll job creation has begun to broaden across various sectors. In 3Q26, average job growth in the private sector was 54,000 per month, slowing from 79,000 per month in 2Q26. For the first time since early 2023, health and education services accounted for less than half of private-sector job growth and manufacturers, wholesale traders, and transportation and warehousing firms saw solid net employment growth.
  - Government payrolls declined slightly in 3Q26, shedding an average of 4,000 jobs per month that was largely due to local governments. Total federal payrolls continued to hold at about 2.68 million workers, down from 3.01 million in January 2025.
- The unemployment rate declined further in 3Q26 to an average of 4.1%—down from averages of 4.3% in the first half of the year. This is well in line with mainstream estimates of the noncyclical unemployment rate—that is, consistent with stable inflation and steady economic growth.
- Wage growth remained solid in the third quarter: over the year through September 2026, nominal average hourly earnings (AHE) for all employees were up 3.0%, and average weekly earnings were up 3.6% over this period. The difference between AHE and AWE growth reflects a small increase in average weekly work hours.
  - The Employment Cost Index (ECI) for all private workers, which controls for compositional changes and includes employee benefits, rose 3.4% over the year ending in September 2026. This was a tick faster than Q2’s pace, reflecting stable wage growth and slightly faster increase in employee benefits.
- Labor force participation declined slightly in 3Q26, partly reflecting ongoing demographic pressures. The overall LFPR slipped to an average of 61.6% in 3Q26 from 61.7% in 2Q26.
  - Although the LFPR among prime-age workers ticked down in 3Q26 to 83.5%, it remained 0.4 percentage points above the previous business cycle peak in January 2020. Participation remains particularly resilient among prime-age men: the LFPR for this group averaged 89.3% in 3Q26, just 0.1 percentage point shy of the previous business cycle peak.
- Monthly job openings averaged 7.2 million in July and August (latest data available), down 0.2 million from 2Q but up from 6.9 million per month in 4Q25 and 1Q26. The ratio of job openings to unemployed persons averaged 1.0 per month in July and August.
- Other indicators reflect labor markets’ ongoing health and stability.
  - The layoff rate remains stable and near historical lows and the hires rate has remained stable since mid-2024.
  - Initial unemployment claims trended down in 3Q26 and remained exceptionally low by historical standards through mid-October.
  - Business applications reached a record high of more than 576,000 in July and remained high through Q3, indicating potential increases in new firm births and associated opportunities for American entrepreneurs.
Inflation
Headline CPI rose 3.7% over the 12 months through September 2026, picking up from the 3.0% annual CPI inflation rate through September 2025. Energy inflation drove roughly 40% of the increase.
- Average headline inflation ticked up to 0.4% per month in 3Q26 from 0.2% in 2Q26 (see Table 3 – Inflation Indicators).
- Energy price inflation accelerated in 3Q26. CPI inflation for energy goods and services averaged 1.9% per month in 3Q26, up from the monthly average of 0.6% in 2Q26 but well below the 3.2% monthly average in 1Q26.
- Food price inflation averaged 0.1% per month in 3Q, down from 0.3% in 2Q, as pressures in the food-at-home category – including beef and coffee prices – receded. Over the 12 months through September, food price inflation was 2.5%, 0.6 percentage points below its year-earlier rate.
Twelve-month core CPI inflation, which excludes the volatile components of food and energy, stood at 2.6% as of September, slowing from the 3.0% rate through September 2025. On a monthly average basis, core inflation ticked up to 0.3% in 3Q26 after averaging 0.2% per month in the first and second quarters.
- Monthly core goods prices increased 0.2% on average in 3Q26, after declining by 0.1% per month in 2Q26. About half of the swing was attributable to new and used motor vehicles, which had flipped from a deflationary to an inflationary force beginning in 2Q. Nonetheless, on a twelve-month basis, core goods inflation was 0.7% through September 2026, the slowest rate since June 2025.
- Rent of housing inflation decelerated to 0.3% per month in 3Q26, down from 0.4% in 2Q26. Rent of housing inflation was 3.2% over the year through September, well below the 3.7% year-earlier rate and slightly below the pre-pandemic average of 3.3%. Inflation for rent of housing services (rent of primary residence and owners’ equivalent rent) has eased since 2024.
- After slowing by half in 2Q26, inflation for non-housing core services averaged 0.4% per month in 3Q26. Most of the acceleration of non-housing core services was due to a pickup in transportation services. Over the year through September 2026, non-housing core services inflation was 3.1%, slowing slightly from the 3.2% year-earlier rate.
The PCE price index has notable differences in weights and methodologies versus the CPI. Over the past 20 years, twelve-month CPI inflation has exceeded PCE inflation by about 0.35 percentage points on average. Over the year through September 2026, headline PCE inflation was 3.6%, above the 2.8% pace over the year through September 2025. The Federal Reserve’s target for headline PCE inflation is 2%.
Risks to the Outlook
Looking ahead to the next few quarters, the outlook for the U.S. economy is favorable and economists view the risk of a recession as low. According to The Wall Street Journal’s survey of economists in October, the average probability of a recession in the next 12 months was just 24%, little changed from 25% in the July survey. The survey also indicated an improved near-term outlook. Projected real GDP growth in 2026 was revised up by 0.3 percentage points to 2.4%, and the expected unemployment rate in December 2026 was revised down to 4.2%. Compared with the July survey, respondents projected slightly higher headline inflation, lower core inflation, and higher interest rates.
Energy prices and geopolitical uncertainty: Geopolitical uncertainty remains a risk to the medium-term inflation outlook. Energy prices are among the most volatile categories of inflation and reflect this uncertainty. Indeed, the energy goods and services CPI fell 1.5% in July but rebounded 2.1% in August and 5.2% in September. The timing, duration, and magnitude of energy price swings contribute to the risk of increased inflation in other goods and services – such as food (through fertilizer and fuel for farming equipment) and airfares – adding uncertainty to the medium-term inflation outlook.
Importantly, the Trump Administration’s policies have made the U.S. economy more resilient to fluctuations in global oil prices. This resilience is due to a wide range of policies enacted, including deregulatory actions that have increased production and exports of oil and gas, and strategic actions abroad that have resulted in increased demand for U.S. crude and increased supply to the U.S. outside of the Middle East. Average domestic crude oil production in 2025 rose by 350,000 barrels per day relative to the 2024 average, and production and exports have risen further in 2026 as U.S. producers continue to build out U.S. infrastructure. The United States is increasingly the world’s largest producer of petroleum products and natural gas, and it is a net exporter of both.
Business fixed investment and the manufacturing outlook: Recent data suggest that the economy is in the early stages of a policy-driven capital-expenditure boom. Since the passage of the Administration’s signature tax bill (the Working Families Tax Cuts), real BFI has risen by a cumulative 9.4% through 3Q26. Provisions in the tax law – such as full expensing of research and development, 100% bonus depreciation for business equipment investments, and restoring deductibility of interest expenses for capital-intensive manufacturers – have contributed to this rapid business investment growth. Indeed, business equipment investment alone has added 0.8 percentage points to GDP growth over the past four quarters, while spending on intellectual property products has contributed 0.5 percentage points.
The tax law also included a temporary provision for full depreciation deduction for the costs of new, nonresidential manufacturing facilities. Although real investment in factories and manufacturing structures has declined since mid-2024, the manufacturing outlook appears favorable. Jobs related to the construction of nonresidential buildings have grown by 116,000 since September 2025, presaging future manufacturing sector growth as new facilities are completed and products are deployed. In addition, firms that manufacture durable goods have increased their payrolls by 101,000 so far this year. Job openings in durable goods manufacturing grew by 93,000, and layoffs and discharges fell by 7,000.
This capital expenditures boom bodes well for future economic growth. Capital expenditures correlate with productivity growth, which is a strategic pillar of the Administration’s economic agenda: productivity growth helps drive stronger economic growth and, as a positive supply-side development, is usually disinflationary while increasing wage growth.
Interest rates: At the end of 2025, the yield on the 10-year Treasury note was 4.18%. As of October 30, it was 76 basis points higher. Several factors may have contributed to this increase, including optimism around U.S. growth expectations alongside higher demand for capital from investments related to SI.
Since last year, economists’ forecasts have improved: the Blue Chip consensus for real GDP growth five years ahead has increased from 1.9% in the October 2025 report to 2.1% in the October 2026 report. Improved growth prospects can lead to higher interest rates as the returns from business investment rise. Increased demand for credit to finance capital investment also correlates with higher interest rates.
The risk to the economic outlook is that higher borrowing costs could worsen the federal debt trajectory. However, U.S. fiscal sustainability does not appear to be a significant driver of the year-to-date increase in interest rates. Rate increases have been a global phenomenon even among countries with lower debt-to-GDP ratios.
Super intelligence (SI): Investment in super intelligence has been a significant driver of economic growth in recent quarters. In the first three quarters of 2026, SI-driven investment (BFI in software, computers and hardware, and data center structures relative to pre-large language models trend) accounted for nearly 30% of GDP growth.
In the long run, firms’ continued investment in super intelligence is likely to lead to efficiency gains, particularly in service-sector industries where productivity growth has been slower. However, the timeline and magnitude of productivity gains are uncertain, as is the ultimate effect on the composition of labor markets. If the integration of super intelligence acts as a standard technology improvement, productivity growth could return to historical norms after a period of above-trend growth. On the other hand, super intelligence could prove transformational and permanently upshift the path of productivity as it enables workers to build skills and human capital faster than in the past.
Labor markets: While labor markets are in balance, labor data indicate an environment of lower job churn than in the past, which could leave the economy with less slack to absorb a negative shock. So far this year, the median private-sector hires rate has been 3.6%, compared to a median of 4.2% in 2019.
By contrast, rates of layoffs and discharges for the private sector have remained near historical lows, with the layoffs rate at just 1.2% in August. The lower turnover environment, while indicating that labor markets are in balance, also suggests a large shock could shift markets out of balance as hiring may not be able to offset an increase in the layoffs and discharges rates.
Conclusion
The U.S. economy remains resilient, and the outlook is favorable. Historically high capital expenditures and steady household consumption growth have increased the economy’s capacity for self-sustaining growth. In the labor market, the unemployment rate and layoffs are low, wages are increasing, and new business applications hit an all-time high. Although energy markets have affected headline inflation, the U.S. economy is resilient to fluctuations in the supply of oil from the Strait of Hormuz, and energy prices should recede following the cessation of conflict in Iran.
The Trump Administration has successfully stewarded major fiscal legislation to prevent a historic tax increase and lower the cost of capital, which has increased return expectations in the market. Since its passage in July 2025, we have seen significant business equipment investment, including industrial equipment. Indeed, current macroeconomic conditions bode well for increasing economic growth as the private sector leads. A net 22% of small businesses report plans to make capital outlays over the next six months, and the Business Roundtable reports that its index of CEO expectations of capital expenditures is now at its highest level since early 2022.
Announced investments in U.S. manufacturing, production, and innovation total trillions of dollars, reflecting global confidence in the United States as a destination for investment. This capital expenditure boom is made possible by the Administration’s policies allowing full expensing of equipment and R&D, tariffs and reshoring incentives, and deregulation. The combined policies of the Trump Administration, both enacted and planned, provide a solid foundation for economic growth and will bring prosperity to all Americans.

Rep. Panetta Announces Over $3.8 Million for Santa Cruz Fire Department Medical Response Vehicle Pilot Program
Santa Cruz, CA – United States Representative Jimmy Panetta (CA-19) announced $3,837,779 in federal funding for the Santa Cruz Fire Department to test a faster, more targeted response to medical emergencies, including traffic crashes. The funding comes from the Safe Streets and Roads for All (SS4A) grant program, which helps improve roadway safety by investing in safety strategies to reduce serious traffic injuries and fatalities.
The project combines two tools to help improve emergency response on Santa Cruz roadways. It will test a cloud-based system that gives emergency vehicles priority at traffic signals, connected to the dispatch system, as well as a smaller medical response vehicle for calls that do not involve a fire, including traffic crashes. The City of Santa Cruz will evaluate whether these tools improve response times and care after crashes, particularly along roads with high rates of serious injuries and key routes to hospitals.
“Every second counts for first responders when it comes to driving on our local roads and highways,” said Rep. Panetta. “This federal investment will allow the city of Santa Cruz to test potentially lifesaving technology to help emergency vehicles reach people more quickly and first responders provide timely, effective care. I’m proud to ensure that the federal government plays its part to help our local first responders do their job for the safety of communities in California’s 19th Congressional District.”
“This grant will allow Santa Cruz to explore new ways to help first responders reach injured patients faster, provide lifesaving care, and improve roadway safety,” said Santa Cruz Mayor Fred Keeley. “I am grateful for Congressman Panetta’s support in delivering this significant federal investment to strengthen emergency response and make our community safer.”
“Keeping our community safe is one of our most important responsibilities, and this investment gives Santa Cruz an exciting opportunity to strengthen how we respond to emergencies. We’re grateful to Congressman Panetta for securing this funding and recognizing the importance of investing in innovative solutions that can help save lives and make our streets safer for everyone. We’re excited to test these tools, evaluate their effectiveness, and identify opportunities to improve service to our community,” said Santa Cruz City Manager Matt Huffaker.
The SS4A grant program was established by the bipartisan Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act in 2021. Since the program’s inception, the cities of Santa Cruz, Monterey, Paso Robles, and San Jose, together with Santa Cruz County, Santa Clara County, the Transportation Agency for Monterey County, and the San Luis Obispo Council of Governments, have received more than $28.7 million through the SS4A program.
Rep. Panetta has previously secured federal investments for a new fire engine in Santa Cruz, pedestrian safety and lighting improvements along Bay Avenue in Capitola, and road safety improvements along Highways 9 and 236 in Boulder Creek.
###
title: Rep. Panetta Announces Over $3.8 Million for Santa Cruz Fire Department Medical Response Vehicle Pilot Program

WASHINGTON, D.C./November 2, 2026 — Today, the U.S. Office of Special Counsel (OSC) notified the President and Congress of the results of a U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) investigation into practices on the acute psychiatric care unit at the Harry S. Truman Memorial Veterans' Hospital in Columbia, Missouri.
A whistleblower raised concerns about how patients were admitted to the unit. The VA Office of the Medical Inspector conducted an on-site investigation in June 2025. The investigation did not substantiate the specific concerns raised, but it uncovered a different issue: the unit's local admission procedures were stricter than what national VA policy allows. Under Veterans Health Administration Directive 1160.06, inpatient mental health care must be available to all eligible veterans who need hospital-level care for a mental health condition.
Investigators also found that some staff mistakenly believed they were authorized to override a provider's decision to admit a patient when assessing how a new patient might affect the unit's environment. This created a risk that veterans who qualified for care could face delays or be turned away. The report also noted that limited training on caring for patients with complex needs, such as dementia, may have made staff reluctant to accept those patients.
In response, the VA adopted three recommendations: revise the unit's procedures to comply with national policy, train staff on the updated process and nurses' role in admissions, and provide clinical training on caring for patients with complex needs. The hospital confirmed that all three have been carried out. The revised procedures were published on July 18, 2025, and the VA's national director for inpatient mental health services found that they comply with national policy.
"We thank the whistleblower for coming forward, "said Special Counsel Charles Baldis. "While the investigation did not substantiate the specific concerns raised, the disclosure revealed a gap between local procedures and national access standards. It also led to meaningful corrective actions that better ensure eligible veterans can receive the inpatient care they need, and that staff are better prepared for complex clinical situations. It is a reminder that whistleblower disclosures can lead to improvements in unexpected ways."
title: Whistleblower Disclosure Leads to Improved Access to Inpatient Mental Health Care at Missouri VA Hospital

Labor Leaders Press Trump Administration on Union-Busting Consultants’ and Corporations’ Compliance with Federal Law
WASHINGTON – Today, House labor leaders demanded information from Office of Labor-Management Standards (OLMS) Director Elisabeth Messenger on whether corporations and their union-busting consultants comply with federal transparency requirements.
The letter was sent by House Education and Workforce Committee Ranking Member Robert C. “Bobby” Scott (VA-03), Subcommittee on Health, Employment, Labor, and Pensions (HELP) Ranking Member Mark DeSaulnier (CA-10), and Education and Workforce Member Rep. Summer L. Lee (PA-12).
Too often, when workers exercise their right to organize a union, corporations and bosses hire outside consultants to wage anti-union campaigns. Over the last several decades, union-avoidance has become a multi-billion-dollar industry. The latest analysis found that companies spend approximately $1.7 billion every year, including nearly $500 million on union-busting consultants, to break their organizing drives. Some consultants are reportedly paid $500 per hour or $4,000 per day for their services.
Under the Labor-Management Reporting and Disclosure Act (LMRDA), employers and consultants are required to file public reports about their matter because it allows workers to see how much their bosses are spending to influence their decision to unionize. However, for decades, employers and union-busting consultants have routinely failed to meet this requirement, allowing bosses and their consultants to operate in the shadows. Under the Trump Administration, the problem is only becoming worse. A recent watchdog report found that, as of August 8, 2026, nearly 60 percent of employers required to file a disclosure in 2025 have still not submitted their reports—the largest year-over-year decline on record.
“Over the last several years, while worker organizing has skyrocketed, employers have increasingly responded with hostile anti-union campaigns, including by hiring well-compensated outside consultants. As more employers seek to quash their workers’ unionization drives, it is imperative that employer and consultant disclosure requirements under the LMRDA are robustly enforced by OLMS, so workers have a complete picture of who is attempting to influence their decision as they exercise their right to organize,” wrote the Members.
To determine whether OLMS is effectively carrying out its responsibility to enforce the LMRDA, the Members requested a response to their extensive questions by no later than November 16, 2026.
To read the full letter to OLMS Director Elisabeth Messenger, click here.

BOSTON – A Rockland man was sentenced today in federal court in Boston for conspiring to distribute fentanyl following a series of controlled drug purchases in Brookline and Boston.

Kerry Charlotin, a/k/a “KG,” 36, of Rockland, was sentenced by U.S. District Court Judge Leo T. Sorokin to 88 months in prison, to be followed by four years of supervised release. In July 2026 , Charlotin pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to distribute fentanyl. Charlotin was arrested and charged in December 2025 along with co-conspirator Shaquylle Burden.

In June 2025, an investigation began into drug trafficking activities conducted by Charlotin and his co-conspirator Burden. The investigation revealed that the defendants were actively trafficking significant quantities of fentanyl and other controlled substances in the greater Boston area.

On various dates in 2025, Charlotin coordinated with Burden and met repeatedly with a federal cooperating witness to conduct controlled sales of fentanyl. During the course of the investigation, Charlotin and Burden sold more than 280 grams of fentanyl, along with other controlled substances.

Following the controlled purchases, search warrants were executed in December 2025, including of Charlotin’s person after he was located and arrested in South Carolina, and at multiple residences in Massachusetts. During the searches, additional cocaine base, a loaded 9mm pistol and approximately 131.5 grams of cocaine were recovered. The cocaine was packaged in plastic bags that had been unsuccessfully attempted to be flushed down a toilet. One firearm was also recovered from Burden’s Roslindale residence at the time of his arrest.

At the time of these offenses, Charlotin was serving a term of supervised release following a prior federal conviction for being a felon in possession of a firearm and ammunition, for which he had previously served a five-year federal prison sentence.

Burden was sentenced to five years in prison for his role in the conspiracy on Oct. 19, 2026 .

United States Attorney Leah B. Foley; Ted E. Docks, Special Agent in Charge of the Federal Bureau of Investigation in Boston; and Boston Police Commissioner Michael Cox made the announcement today. Valuable assistance was provided by the FBI’s Columbia Field Office in South Carolina. Assistant U.S. Attorney John T. Dawley of the Organized Crime & Gang Unit is prosecuting the case.

This case is part of Operation Take Back America a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations, and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime.
title: Rockland Man Sentenced to More Than Seven Years in Prison for Drug Conspiracy

Washington, D.C. — Today, Rep. Robert Garcia, Ranking Member of the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, demanded answers from Secretary of State Marco Rubio after the Trump Administration allegedly helped bring Flávio Bolsonaro, a Brazilian politician under investigation for money laundering and corruption, into the United States.
“Donald Trump appears to have no problem pulling out all the stops for a far-right Brazilian politician who lost his election and is under investigation for corruption. Secretary Rubio should send Bolsonaro home to face justice and fully explain why this Administration helped bring him here. We are demanding answers,” said Ranking Member Robert Garcia.
In the letter to Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Ranking Member Garcia wrote, “While President Trump uses ICE as his personal police force to terrorize kids and hardworking people trying to support their families and communities, he has bent over backwards to bring to the U.S. Flávio Bolsonaro, a disgraced Brazilian politician under investigation for money laundering, corruption, and other serious crimes. If the President claims he doesn’t want criminals to come to the U.S., why allow Mr. Bolsonaro entry? Trump Administration officials’ ties to Mr. Bolsonaro—including your own—cast doubt on the motives for giving him such special treatment. The fact that Vice President Vance’s former firm has connections to one of the ongoing criminal investigations raises further questions about political considerations in this process. You should immediately return Mr. Bolsonaro to Brazil to face justice and be prepared to explain why the Trump Administration is welcoming a corrupt politician and government official fleeing accountability into our country while terrorizing Americans and lawful residents of the U.S. that you have falsely labeled as criminals.”
In September 2026, Ranking Member Robert Garcia demanded answers from Secretary Rubio and Attorney General Todd Blanche after they allegedly helped white collar criminal Alejandro Betancourt lead the Trump Administration’s unprecedented scheme to take an ownership stake in a Venezuelan oil company.
In August 2025, Ranking Member Garcia demanded answers following reports that President Trump and Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele entered into a secret, backdoor deal that resulted in America’s release of dangerous MS-13 leaders back to El Salvador.

WASHINGTON – The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) kicks off Critical Infrastructure and Resilience Month today, recognizing the systems and assets that keep the country running as well as the people who operate them. This year’s Critical Infrastructure Security and Resilience Month aligns with President Trump’s National Resilience Strategy and comes as we continue to see new and evolving threats, including those driven by rapid advances in technology like super intelligence. Through it all, we rely on frontline operators who keep essential services moving even when things are disrupted.
“Our work depends on people who understand their systems and stay prepared,” said Acting CISA Director Nick Andersen. “Resilience comes from knowing what matters most and having a plan you can actually use when something goes wrong.”
All month, CISA will highlight four practices that help infrastructure owners and operators stay prepared:
- Know your most important systems and the outside services they depend on
- Understand the risks that matter most to your organization
- Make clear plans that guide response and recovery
- Track progress and update plans based on real lessons learned
As threats continue to emerge, it’s imperative that everyone does their part to be more resilient. Strong resilience in critical infrastructure helps protect lives and jobs, keeps communities connected, and reduces disruptions. Critical Infrastructure Security and Resilience Month empowers American industry, state and local governments, and the Federal Government to each do their part to protect our nation’s security, prosperity, and freedom.
Organizations can participate in Critical Infrastructure Security and Resilience Month with CISA’s toolkit, which includes graphics and plain language text that organizations can use to show the steps they are taking this November to be more resilient.
###
About CISA
As the nation’s cyber defense agency and national coordinator for critical infrastructure security, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency leads the national effort to manage, uncover, and reduce risk to our digital and physical infrastructure Americans rely on every hour of every day.
Visit CISA.gov for more information and follow us on X, Facebook, LinkedIn, Instagram.
title: CISA Kicks Off Critical Infrastructure Security and Resilience Month 2026

PHILADELPHIA – FEMA will evaluate a Biennial Radiological Emergency Preparedness Exercise at the Salem & Hope Creek Nuclear Generating Stations. The exercise will occur during the week of Nov. 16, 2026, to assess and improve the ability of the state of Delaware to respond to an emergency at the nuclear facility.
“These drills are held every other year to evaluate government’s ability to protect public health and safety,” said Andre C. McCoy, Regional Administrator for FEMA Region 3. “We will assess state and local government emergency response capabilities within the 10-mile Emergency Planning Zone and the 50-mile Ingestion Pathway Zone in the state of Delaware.”
Within 90 days, FEMA will send its evaluation to the Nuclear Regulatory Commission for use in licensing decisions. The final report will be available to the public approximately 120 days after the exercise.
FEMA will present preliminary findings of the exercise during a public meeting at 12:30 pm EST on Friday, Nov. 20, 2026. Planned speakers include representatives from FEMA and the Nuclear Regulatory Commission. The meeting will take place in-person at:
SpringHill Suites by Marriott Frederica
208 Dominus Drive 
Frederica, DE 19946
At the public meeting, FEMA may request that questions or comments be submitted in writing for review and response. Written comments may also be submitted after the meeting by emailing FEMAR3NewsDesk@fema.dhs.gov or by mail to:
Andre C. McCoy, Regional Administrator
FEMA Region 3
615 Chestnut Street, 6th Floor
Philadelphia, PA  19106
FEMA created the Radiological Emergency Preparedness Program to ensure that residents living near commercial nuclear power plants would be adequately protected in the event of a nuclear power plant accident. The program also helps inform and educate the public about radiological emergency preparedness.
Radiological Emergency Preparedness Program responsibilities cover only “offsite” activities: state and local government emergency planning and preparedness activities that take place beyond the nuclear power plant boundaries. Onsite activities continue to be the responsibility of the Nuclear Regulatory Commission.
Additional information on FEMA’s Radiological Emergency Preparedness Program is available online at FEMA.gov/Radiological-Emergency-Preparedness-Program.
If you have questions, please contact the FEMA Region 3 Office of External Affairs at femar3newsdesk@fema.dhs.gov.
###
FEMA’s mission is helping people before, during and after disasters.
Follow FEMA online, on X @FEMA or @FEMAEspanol, on FEMA's Facebook page or Espanol page, on Truth Social and FEMA's YouTube account.
For preparedness information, follow the Ready Campaign on X at @Ready.gov, on Instagram @Ready.gov or on the Ready Facebook page
