PITTSBURGH, Pa. – A resident of Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, pleaded guilty in federal court to one count of false impersonation of a federal officer or employee, United States Attorney Troy Rivetti announced today.

Lazaven Mitchell, 38, pleaded guilty before Senior United States District Judge David Stewart Cercone.

In connection with the guilty plea, the Court was advised that Mitchell is a Pittsburgh-based licensed financial advisor and loan officer who, on multiple occasions between April 2024 and June 2024, presented himself to local businesses as working for the U.S. Department of Labor’s Employee Benefits Security Administration (EBSA). Mitchell would contact Pittsburgh businesses, identify himself as working for EBSA, and request to review the businesses’ retirement plans to determine whether they were in compliance with authorities governing retirement plans.

After reviewing a retirement plan, Mitchell would identify a compliance issue and then recommend that the business terminate its current advisor and transfer the plan to him to serve as the plan administrator, including providing the business owner with a draft letter for their signature that would terminate the old plan advisor. To effectuate this, Mitchell would send a letter to the business bearing the Department of Labor seal and EBSA mailing address in Washington D.C. In text messages between Mitchell and one business owner, Mitchell referenced having “a final determination from the DOL,” and to coming to the business to retrieve “the documents for the Department of Labor inquiry.” In a text to a different business owner, Mitchell sent a fictitious business card bearing the EBSA’s name and crest, his name with the title of “Employee Benefit Advisor,” and an address for a suite within the William S. Moorhead Federal Building.

Judge Cercone scheduled sentencing for March 25, 2027. The law provides for a total maximum sentence of up to three years in prison, a fine of up to the greater of $250,000 or twice the gross pecuniary gain to Mitchell, or both. Under the federal Sentencing Guidelines, the actual sentence imposed is based upon the seriousness of the offense and the prior criminal history, if any, of the defendant.

Assistant United States Attorney Brendan J. McKenna is prosecuting this case on behalf of the government.

The Federal Bureau of Investigation and U.S. Department of Labor Office of Inspector General conducted the investigation that led to the prosecution of Mitchell.
title: Pittsburgh Financial Advisor Pleads Guilty to Falsely Impersonating Department of Labor Employee

EPA Proposal Would Deliver Strategic Win for Energy Dominance, Economic Growth in Alaska
SEATTLE – On October 27, 2026, EPA announced a proposal to approve Alaska’s request to administer permitting under the Safe Drinking Water Act for Class VI underground injection wells in the state. This action recognizes that states are best positioned to protect their underground sources of drinking water while advancing economic growth, cooperative federalism, and energy dominance.
“At the Trump EPA, we believe that the people of Alaska know their energy needs and how to protect their air, land, and water better than anyone sitting in an office building in Washington, DC,” said EPA Region 10 Administrator Emma Pokon. “This proposal, if finalized, would uphold the agency’s commitment to cooperative federalism and advance American energy dominance by giving Alaska the ability to produce more energy while protecting underground sources of drinking water.”
With this action, EPA is proposing to grant Alaska primary enforcement responsibility, or “primacy,” for Class VI wells that are used to inject carbon dioxide (CO2) from sources such as industrial processes and energy production into deep underground rock formations. Based on EPA’s preliminary review of the state’s application for primacy, this action proposes that Alaska’s Underground Injection Control program meets all requirements for approval and that the state would implement and enforce the program consistent with the Act.
EPA is seeking comment on this proposed action for 45 days, and will host a virtual public hearing.
If finalized, EPA’s approval of Alaska’s UIC Class VI primacy application would allow the Alaska Oil and Gas Conservation Commission (AOGCC) to issue and enforce compliance with UIC Class VI permits for injection wells used for geologic carbon sequestration.
"The AOGCC values its strong working relationship with the EPA and looks forward to continuing that collaboration,” said AOGCC Commissioner Jessie Chmielowski. "Together with other State of Alaska agencies, we believe that securing Class VI primacy will build on our existing Class II regulatory expertise and help ensure the safe, responsible, and compliant development of geologic carbon storage projects in Alaska."
Since 2025, EPA has approved Class VI primacy for West Virginia, Texas, Arizona, and Colorado while committing to expediting review of UIC primacy applications and review of permits issued by the agency. This primacy proposal would further fulfill this commitment. To date, seven states have received primacy for Class VI wells with more coming under President Trump’s leadership. This work was made possible in part by funding provided to EPA through an interagency agreement with the Federal Permitting Improvement Steering Council (Permitting Council).
title: EPA Proposal Would Deliver Strategic Win for Energy Dominance, Economic Growth in Alaska

WASHINGTON — Seeking to disrupt how the military funds modernization, Marc Andersen, Assistant Secretary of the Army for Financial Management and Comptroller, declared that the service must "move at the speed of capitalism" to outpace global adversaries. Speaking at the Association of the United States Army 2026 Annual Meeting, Oct. 15, 2026, Andersen championed the Strategic Capital Initiative as a permanent institutional shift to align national security priorities with commercial business cases.
Throughout the panel discussion, Andersen reinforced that SCI is not just another pilot program, but a fundamental shift in how the Army approaches public-private collaboration. A primary focus of his remarks was the concept of de-risking investments for public-private partnerships to create certainty for both the warfighter and the investor. Andersen explained that private capital requires financial predictability the same as military requires operational certainty that a capability will work when needed. By leveraging creative, long-term enhanced use leases, the Army can provide the stable environment necessary to attract significant private investment, effectively aligning national security priorities with commercial business cases.
To execute this vision, Andersen stressed that the Army must operate at the "speed of capitalism" rather than relying on rigid, transactional procurement models. He called for a shoulder-to-shoulder collaboration model grounded in open, early communication where both sides can discuss constraints honestly. This cultural shift requires a significant investment of time and energy to build mutual understanding, which Andersen argued is the only way to move fast enough to counter modern strategic adversaries.
Equally important to this mission is the institutional endurance of the initiative itself. Andersen noted that while individual leaders are only in their roles for a brief period, the structures established by the SCI must outlive them to create a permanent, healthier, and more diverse industrial base. To ensure this long-term success, his team is actively working to overcome legacy bureaucracy by carefully distinguishing between actual statutory laws and mere historical norms or policy behaviors that have frozen procurement processes over time.
By aggressively challenging these internal preferences, the Army aims to create a frictionless pathway that avoids the slow, bureaucratic traps of the past. Andersen said “We’re actively hunting policy, to reduce friction, increase velocity and move at the speed of trust to properly resource our Army to fight and win or nation’s wars. As we rebuild our Arsenal of Democracy, we are grounded in deterrence while ensuring our Warfighters never enter a fair fight.”
title: Transforming defense finance: Andersen champions speed, trust, and endurance at AUSA 2026

PHILADELPHIA – United States Attorney David Metcalf announced that five Philadelphia men were sentenced to prison last week by United States District Judge John F. Murphy for conspiring to commit dozens of armed carjackings in and around Philadelphia and selling the stolen cars to buyers, and numerous related violent offenses.

The defendants were charged by superseding indictment in July of 2024 and convicted at trial in March of this year after an eight-week trial, that included over 100 witnesses and significant technical and scientific evidence.

Mikal McCracken , a/k/a “Kal,” age 24, was sentenced to life plus 138 years in prison.

At trial, McCracken was convicted of carjacking resulting in death and related offenses, where he and three others carjacked and killed a former Marine in February of 2022. During the carjacking, McCracken shot the victim several times and killed him. McCracken was also convicted of counts related to his participation in a conspiracy, with two others, to murder a potential witness in February of 2022, whom the conspirators feared might be able to provide evidence against the conspiracy regarding the carjacking resulting in death of the former marine. In addition, McCracken was convicted for offenses related to an additional 19 armed attempted or completed carjackings, and a 20 th carjacking was also included as part of his participation in the conspiracy offense. Those armed carjackings included five where victims were shot or shot at. One of these victims was carjacked and shot in the same leg on two separate occasions a month apart.

Amin Muse , a/k/a “Miyn” and “Miyns,” age 24, was sentenced to life plus 55 years in prison.

At trial, Muse was convicted of carjacking resulting in death and related offenses, where he and three others carjacked and killed a former Marine in February of 2022. Muse was also convicted of counts related to his participation in the conspiracy, with two others, to murder the potential witness, whom the conspirators feared might be able to provide evidence against the conspiracy regarding the carjacking resulting in death of the former marine. In addition, Muse was convicted for offenses related to an additional 10 armed attempted or completed carjackings. Those 10 armed carjackings included one where the victim was shot at, and one where the victim was shot in the hand and the foot.

Aleem Abdul-Hakim , a/k/a “Fatleem,” age 23, was sentenced to life plus 28 years in prison.

At trial, Abdul-Hakim was convicted of carjacking resulting in death and related offenses, where he and three others carjacked and killed a former Marine in February of 2022. Abdul-Hakim was also convicted of offenses related to an additional 5 armed attempted or completed carjackings.

Dean Fosque , a/k/a “30,” age 28, was sentenced to 86 years in prison and five years of supervised release.

At trial, Fosque was convicted of offenses related to 10 armed carjackings, which included three shootings, where one of those three victims was hit.

Kavon Coleman , a/k/a “Ski,” age 24, was sentenced to 35 years in prison and five years of supervised release.

At trial, Coleman was convicted of offenses related to four armed attempted or completed carjackings, which included one shooting where the victim of the attempted carjacking was shot in the leg — and that victim had been a previous victim of this conspiracy about a month earlier, where he was carjacked and shot in the same leg.

“The rampant and senseless violence wrought by this carjacking crew demanded a strong response — on both the victims’ and the community’s behalf,” said U.S. Attorney Metcalf. “The Philadelphia Carjacking Task Force will continue to pool the resources and intelligence needed to get the city’s most violent offenders off the street and behind bars. As these defendants’ sentences show, if you commit carjackings here and terrorize innocent people, expect to become a long-term resident in one of our federal prisons.”

As detailed in court filings and proven at trial, between October 2021 and October 2022, groups of rotating carjackers, including McCracken, Muse, Abdul-Hakim, Fosque, Coleman, and others, committed dozens of gunpoint carjackings, often carrying out multiple carjackings in one night. Many of these crimes occurred in Southwest and Northeast Philadelphia, and there were also carjackings in the surrounding suburbs, including Yeadon, Millbourne, Lower Southampton, and King of Prussia.

The carjackers used firearms and often assaulted their victims, sometimes by shooting them. In addition to cars, they also took personal identification, credit cards, and money from their victims. In several cases, conspirators then used the stolen identification materials to commit fraud crimes.

In all, the conspiracy involved approximately 60 carjackings, 30 of which were charged in the superseding indictment, two of which were presented as overt acts of the conspiracy. The conspiracy also included the additional carjacking which resulted in the murder of the victim, and the second murder of the potential witness. The charges included numerous shootings, including four shootings that left the victims (one of whom had been carjacked and shot on two different occasions) seriously injured.

The first murder occurred on February 6, 2022, when McCracken, Muse, and Abdul-Hakim, along with Jonathan Akubu, charged elsewhere, carjacked Victim 1, and shot and killed him in the process. McCracken, Muse, and Abdul-Hakim approached Victim 1 with guns and demanded his car, while Akubu waited on another block in the car used by the offenders. During the carjacking McCracken shot and killed Victim 1.

In their haste to flee the scene in Victim 1’s car, which was already running, the carjackers failed to take Victim 1’s key fob, which they would need to continue operating the stolen car after it was eventually shut off. Accordingly, they enlisted the help of a locksmith (Victim 2) to make them a new key for the car.

Shortly after the key was made, the police located and recovered Victim 1’s vehicle. McCracken, Muse, and Akubu feared that law enforcement would identify the locksmith through forensics, because he touched the car while making the replacement key. The three believed that if identified, the locksmith would then cooperate with law enforcement investigating the killing and lead investigators toward the conspiracy, so they agreed to kill Victim 2 and they all planned his murder, which Akubu carried out on behalf of the conspirators on February 12, 2022.

The investigation revealed that the carjackers, who usually operated in smaller groups of two to four, had been responsible for numerous carjackings dating as far back as October of 2021. The defendants conspired with each other and other conspirators to sell these carjacked cars to buyers overseas. Several of the carjacked cars taken during this conspiracy were discovered in shipping containers bound for countries abroad.

“The brazen and deadly acts of violence in this case shattered lives, devastated families, and threatened the safety and well-being of Philadelphia communities,” said Wayne A. Jacobs, Special Agent in Charge of FBI Philadelphia. “While no sentence can undo the harm inflicted, this outcome reflects the tireless work of the FBI Violent Crimes Task Force and our law enforcement partners to hold those responsible accountable. At the center of our efforts are the victims, those whose lives were tragically cut short, the loved ones left behind, and the survivors forever changed by these senseless acts. These sentences are a measure of justice for them and a reflection of our unwavering commitment to combating violent crime and making Philadelphia safer for everyone who calls this city home.”

“This case represented some of the very worst of what we saw during the rise of violent carjackings: calculated, coordinated, and completely indifferent to human life,” said Philadelphia Police Commissioner Kevin J. Bethel. “These individuals didn’t just steal cars — they terrorized neighborhoods, took innocent lives, and attempted to silence witnesses to cover their crimes. Thanks to the relentless work of the Philadelphia Police Department and our federal partners, this violent crew has been dismantled and held accountable. Let this be clear: if you bring this level of violence to our city, we will bring the full weight of law enforcement down on you. At the same time, we are seeing real progress: violent crime, including carjackings, continues to trend down because of the dedication of our officers and the strength of these partnerships. This is what the work looks like, and we are not slowing down.”

“ATF protects our communities from violent crime, and these sentences close the book on one of the most extensive and terrible carjacking rings in American history,” said ATF Philadelphia Field Division Special Agent in Charge Eric DeGree. “Through the teamwork of the Philadelphia Carjacking Task Force, we brought these brazen criminals to justice. Their prison sentences should be a deterrent to those who think they can terrorize this city with carjackings, murder, and witness intimidation.”

“These convictions should send a loud message to auto thieves that CBP and our law enforcement partners will continue to treat violent carjacking as a serious public safety threat and will hold perpetrators accountable. CBP continues to combat transnational criminal organizations by intercepting stolen vehicle exports at our nation’s ports of entry and depriving criminal gangs of this illicit revenue,” said Elliot N. Ortiz, CBP’s Area Port Director in Philadelphia.

“HSI Philadelphia, working closely with our law enforcement partners, identified and disrupted the overseas trafficking of vehicles stolen through this violent carjacking conspiracy,” said HSI Philadelphia Special Agent in Charge Nathan Abel. “Today’s sentences hold these defendants accountable not only for the vehicles they stole, but for the devastating violence they inflicted on victims and the Philadelphia community. HSI remains committed to using our global reach and investigative expertise alongside our partners to combat transnational criminal activity and protect the public.”

This case was investigated by the Philadelphia Carjacking Task Force, comprising the FBI, Philadelphia Police Department, and Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, with significant assistance from the Philadelphia offices of Customs and Border Protection and Homeland Security Investigations, which helped investigate and uncover carjacked cars meant to be exported overseas. The case was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorneys Joseph LaBar and Katherine Shulman.
title: Three Philadelphia Men Sentenced to Life in Prison, Two Others to Decades Behind Bars, for Conspiring to Commit and Committing the Murder of a Carjacking Victim, Murder of a Potential Witness, and Approximately 30 Additional Carjackings, Related Offenses

ADELPHI, Md. — Years of Army scientific research culminated in the successful flight demonstration of a 3D-printed heavy-fuel rotary-engine series-hybrid system, advancing power and propulsion science for future tactical unmanned aircraft systems.
Researchers at the U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command, known as DEVCOM, Army Research Laboratory, designed the advanced drone propulsion through its Versatile Tactical Power and Propulsion essential research program.
"The program addresses critical power and propulsion challenges by advancing fundamental science that could enable drones to fly longer and faster, operate at higher altitudes, carry heavier payloads and perform in extreme environments while reducing logistics burdens," said Dr. Chol-Bum “Mike” Kweon, DEVCOM ARL program manager. "For warfighters, the program has transitioned research findings to industry partners for maturation and integration into capabilities that could enable mid-sized drones to operate beyond line of sight, extending the reach of ground commanders and reducing risk to Soldiers."
ARL researchers used advanced computational fluid dynamics modeling and a clean-sheet design approach to address the challenges of efficiently burning heavy fuel in a rotary engine. The work improved fuel atomization and vaporization while minimizing compressed-air and fuel-vapor leaks.
“The use of advanced manufacturing, including 3D metal printing, allowed us to rapidly redesign engine components based on lessons learned through experimentation,” Kweon said. “It enabled us to design an air-cooled engine that reduces propulsion-system size and eliminates the need for liquid coolant.”
Integrated with a novel 400-volt motor-generator system, the engine forms a heavy-fuel rotary-engine series-hybrid system designed to support vertical takeoff and landing operations in contested environments.
To demonstrate the propulsion system in flight, ARL worked with industry partners, including Griffon Aerospace, to develop an aircraft platform around the propulsion system. The novel series hybrid system powers the Group 3 midsized, unmanned aircraft system, Versatile Intelligence Controlled Tactical Operational Reconnaissance and Attack, or VICTOR UAS.
The VICTOR essential research program generated many additional outcomes for the Army, industry and academia, including:
- Collaborative research with more than 30 universities, more than 13 federal laboratories and more than 20 industry partners that resulted in hundreds of scientific journal publications in diverse areas including combustion chemistry, sensing and controls, material design, batteries and hybrid electric technology
- Professionally developed hundreds of scientists and engineers now working in government, industry and academia
- Research advances that address energy and propulsion challenges relevant to tactical-level energy independence
- Technical data packages, design methods and reliability lessons applicable to future propulsion and drone design and integration efforts
- Tens of patents and patent applications
Lessons from the essential research program will inform follow-on ARL research and industry development efforts, including the Persistent Unmanned Aircraft System for Logistics, Strike, Autonomy, and Reconnaissance, or PULSAR, an advanced drone-operation concept that enables multi-mission capabilities through a swarm of VICTOR drones.
The VICTOR UAS and the PULSAR concept will be made available to military partners for further experimentation and development. Industry partners will continue refining VICTOR UAS for other applications.
─────────────────────────
DEVCOM ARL is the Army’s sole fundamental research laboratory serving as the nexus of science between the military, academia and industry. Operating under the U.S. Army Futures and Autonomous Systems Command, ARL executes globally recognized research to accelerate delivery of war-winning, disruptive technologies for tomorrow’s Army.
For information, visit the Army Research Laboratory website.
title: Army research leads to first 3D-printed heavy-fuel engine

SACRAMENTO, Calif. — Federal prosecutors filed criminal complaints charging six aliens with illegally voting in the 2024 U.S. presidential election, U.S. Attorney Grant announced.

“These complaints reflect the seriousness with which the United States government strives to protect the privileges of American citizenship,” said U.S. Attorney Grant. “The right to vote is one of the most fundamental of those privileges, and its theft by noncitizens will be prosecuted.”

Case details are as follows:

Lorie Jane Alcala, 44, a Philippine national residing in Hanford, is charged with illegally voting in the U.S. presidential election on Nov. 5, 2024. Alcala made her initial appearance in federal court on Oct. 30, 2026.

Edith San Pedro Carter, 59, a Philippine national residing in Fresno, is charged with illegally voting in the U.S. presidential election on Nov. 5, 2024. Carter made her initial appearance in federal court on Oct. 30, 2026.

Maria Joao Bettencourt, 49, a Portuguese national residing in Visalia, is charged with illegally voting in the U.S. presidential election on Nov. 5, 2024. Bettencourt will make her initial appearance in federal court on Nov. 2, 2026, in Fresno at 2:00 pm.

Rosa Bento Silva Anderson, 26, a Portuguese national residing in Turlock, is charged with illegally voting in the U.S. presidential election on Nov. 5, 2024. Anderson will make her initial appearance in federal court on Nov. 2, 2026, in Fresno at 2:00 pm.

Janelyn Stewart, 38, a Philippine national residing in Vallejo, is charged with illegally voting in the U.S. presidential election on Nov. 5, 2024.

Meryll Joy Quirong Costi, 36, a Philippine national residing in Sacramento, is charged with illegally voting in the Nov. 5, 2024, presidential election and the Nov. 8, 2022, midterm election. Costi is scheduled to make her initial appearance in federal court on Nov. 2, 2026, in Sacramento at 2 pm.

The Federal Bureau of Investigation and Homeland Security Investigations conducted the investigations. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Joshua Banister and Kevin Khasigian are prosecuting the case.

If convicted, the defendants face a maximum penalty of one year in prison and a fine of up to $100,000. Any sentence, however, would be determined at the discretion of the court after consideration of any applicable statutory factors and the federal Sentencing Guidelines, which take into account a number of variables. The charges are only allegations; the defendants are presumed innocent until and unless proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt.
title: Six Additional Aliens Charged with Illegal Voting in the Counties of Fresno, Kings, Sacramento, Solano, Stanislaus, and Tulare

text:
Peters Urges Trump Admin to Cancel Mass Deportation Flights to Afghanistan and Iran
November 2, 2026 
“We are extremely concerned that sending vulnerable people who sought safety in the U.S. to Afghanistan or Iran will result in their persecution, torture, or even death.”
San Diego, CA. — Today, U.S. Representative Scott Peters (CA-50) led 65 bicameral Members of Congress on a letter to Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin, demanding the immediate cancellation of any deportation flights carrying Afghans and Iranians, whether sent directly or through another country.  
This letter comes after reports that over 150 Afghans could be deported to Pakistan in the coming days, which would constitute one of the largest single expulsions of Afghans ever. San Diego has served as a primary hub for incoming Afghan refugees, with nearly 5,000 resettling in the region. The Members also expressed concern over another flight with a mass deportation of Iranians — the first since the U.S. launched its military conflict against Iran— and that relatives of Afghans who helped American troops could be among those on board. 
“Our nation made a promise to stand by Afghans who risked their lives and their families’ safety to stand by U.S. service members,” the Members wrote, adding that deporting them “is a violation of that promise and our moral obligations to the Afghan community who stood alongside our troops.” 
The Members emphasized the well-documented danger awaiting deportees. The State Department lists Afghanistan as a Level 4 “Do Not Travel” country, and for those who aided U.S. forces, “their assistance to U.S. troops puts a target on these individuals and their families to this day.” They detail the torture, detention, and extrajudicial killing of dissidents and LGBTQ persons, as well as the severe repression of women — noting that women and LGBTQ refugees could be on the flight. 
The Members also raised alarm over reports that Iranians, including women, Christian converts, and pro-democracy activists, may be deported to Iran, where they face imprisonment, torture, and a possible death sentence. “Sending people who sought protection from the Islamic Republic of Iran back to a war zone and a repressive regime is unconscionable,” they wrote. They cited how even President Trump has warned about the dangers faced by pro-democracy and anti-government protesters in Iran. 
The Members stressed that routing a flight through a third country does not change U.S. obligations, and urged the Trump Administration to warn Pakistan that the U.S. will not accept its participation in sending deportees onward to the Taliban. 
These individuals “came to the U.S. because they believed in its promise of democracy, religious freedom, and liberty,” the Members concluded, and “we must uphold those values and commitments, not abandon people to autocratic regimes.” 
“Sixty-six members of Congress, from both chambers, needed less than 24 hours to say what every veteran of the Afghanistan war already knows: you don’t hand the people who stood with our troops to the Taliban. When even the Taliban are voicing ‘serious concern’ about your deportation plan, you’ve lost the moral argument and the national security one. This flight isn’t immigration enforcement. It’s a betrayal with a boarding pass, and the whole world is watching whether America keeps its word. We are grateful to Rep. Peters for leading. Secretary Rubio and Secretary Mullin, ground this plane,” said Shawn VanDiver, U.S. Navy veteran and President and Founder of #AfghanEvac. 
"Having effectively dismantled our protection system, this administration is set to deport vulnerable people back to Afghanistan and Iran, in violation of our human rights commitments and our nation's values," said Sarah Mehta, deputy director of immigration policy at the ACLU. "So many of these men and women never had a meaningful opportunity to defend their claims and are now the casualties of this administration's assault on asylum. We thank Congressman Peters for his leadership and all the members standing against these unconscionable deportations back to persecution, torture, or even death."   
Background:  
San Diego has served as a primary hub for incoming Afghan refugees, and Rep. Peters has been a staunch advocate for the safe relocation, protection, and legal adjustment of Afghan wartime allies who served alongside U.S. forces. He is a cosponsor of the Enduring Welcome Act to codify the Office of the Coordinator for Afghan Relocation Efforts (CARE) within the State Department, and the Afghan Adjustment Act to help settle Afghans and their families who supported U.S. forces. 
In September, Rep. Peters led a Congressional delegation on a letter to the Trump Administration urging them to reunite the families of U.S. service members with their loved ones stranded overseas, and to reconnect Afghans with immediate family already lawfully in the U.S. In July, he hosted a virtual town hall with Afghan allies stranded at the Camp As Sayliyah facility in Doha. And in February, Rep. Peters attended a shadow hearing where he highlighted the consequences of the Trump administration's decisions to freeze the U.S. refugee admissions program and eliminate Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for Afghans. 
###
title: Peters Urges Trump Admin to Cancel Mass Deportation Flights to Afghanistan and Iran

Salinas, Bonamici, Merkley, Wyden Secure over $500,000 for Tualatin Soil and Water Conservation District
Tualatin, OR — Today, Congresswomen Andrea Salinas (OR-06) and Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01), alongside Oregon Senators Ron Wyden and Jeff Merkley, announced they secured the release of over $530,000 in federal funding from the Natural Resources Conservation Service (NRCS) to support Tualatin Soil and Water Conservation District (TSWCD).
In 2022, TSWCD applied to the NRCS for funding to improve fish habitat in Washington County. This work included replacing deteriorated culverts with bridges and modern culverts that help threatened species like steelhead trout move through local waterways. In February 2024, NRCS approved and obligated $1,074,887 to reimburse TSWCD for their work.
As of early September 2026, NRCS had only paid $543,837 of the over $1.07 million they had promised to TSWCD. This $531,000 shortfall has severely challenged TSWCD’s budget and would have stuck the taxpayers of Washington County with the bill. Following outreach from the Oregon delegation, NRSC honored its commitment and released the final sum to TSWCD.
“When Oregonians make a promise, we keep it. The federal government should be held to the same standard,” said Rep. Salinas. “Tualatin Soil and Water did the work to improve our waterways, and Washington County taxpayers should never have been left holding the bag. I’m glad we got this money out the door and where it belongs.”
“Supporting threatened species and their habitats reflects Oregon values and our commitment to environmental protection, and I was grateful when the Tualatin Soil and Water Conservation District secured federal funds to improve fish habitat in Washington County,” said Rep. Bonamici. “Unfortunately, the Trump administration paid only about half of the promised funding, leaving Washington County taxpayers to pick up the balance. I’m glad that my colleagues and I were able to help resolve this issue and secure all the funds the water conservation district needed for the project."
“Thanks to our efforts, this funding is finally moving forward and will help ensure the Tualatin Soil and Water Conservation District can continue its work to improve waterways in Washington County,” said Sen. Merkley.“Oregon’s native fish are the lifeblood of our state, supporting the health and vitality of our communities, local economies, and Tribes who have been here since time immemorial. I’ll keep pushing to secure the necessary federal funds to protect our state’s ecosystems for generations to come.”
“I’m glad the full-court press by the delegation unlocked these resources promised by the federal government to the Tualatin Soil and Water Conservation District,” Wyden said. “These funds will keep waterways improvements on track, helping with water quality and fish habitat alike in Washington County.”
“The Tualatin Soil and Water Conservation District much appreciates Congresswoman Salinas and her staff for their work in helping the District receive payment from the U.S. Department of Agriculture for a successful fish habitat project in the Gales Creek watershed of Washington County,” said Dean P. Moberg, Tualatin Soil and Water Conservation District Treasurer. “We were impressed with the staff's quick understanding of the payment problem we faced, and we are grateful for the Congresswoman's exceptional response. The letter Congresswoman Salinas provided, along with Congresswoman Bonamici and Senators Merkley and Wyden, was surely instrumental in cutting through red tape and securing the payment of over one half million dollars in federal assistance that had been held up for this project. This payment will greatly facilitate the Tualatin Soil and Water Conservation District's work in helping residents of Washington County conserve natural resources with voluntary and locally led projects.

title: Salinas, Bonamici, Merkley, Wyden Secure over $500,000 for Tualatin Soil and Water Conservation District

Remarks

Ambassador Rabbi Yehuda Kaploun, Special Envoy to Monitor and Combat Antisemitism Office of the Special Envoy to Monitor and Combat Antisemitism

Buenos Aires, Argentina

November 1, 2026

As Prepared.

Thank you, Ambassador Fabiana Loguzzo, Mr. Marcelo Mindlin, Secretary General Michaela Küchler, Israel’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Latino Coalition for Israel, and the Latin American Jewish Congress for hosting this important convening.

Just minutes from this room, the Jewish diaspora suffered its deadliest terrorist attack since the Holocaust. On July 18, 1994, Iranian-backed Hizballah terrorists bombed the AMIA Jewish community center. They murdered 85 innocent people and wounded more than 300. Thirty-two years later, the victims’ families, the Argentine people, and Jewish communities around the world are still seeking justice.

It means something that we gather here, under Argentina’s historic IHRA presidency, to discuss the role of the state in combating antisemitism. Once a refuge for Nazi war criminals and a bastion of antisemitic terror, Argentina has shown us what happens when a government decides to act. Under my good friend President Milei, and together with Foreign Minister Quirno, Argentina has designated Hamas and the IRGC as terrorist organizations; pursued a trial in absentia against the perpetrators of the AMIA terrorist attack; and hosted the launch of the U.S.-led Global Guidelines for Countering Antisemitism.

Argentina stands together with the United States in leading boldly and unapologetically to protect Jewish communities worldwide. Under President Trump and Secretary Rubio, the United States is reversing four years of bureaucratic handwringing and shameful inaction by acting decisively to protect Jewish communities. We have confronted antisemitism on university campuses; reinvigorated hate crime prosecutions; implemented rigorous visa vetting to prevent foreign nationals from fomenting hatred; withdrawn from antisemitic international organizations and held UNRWA accountable; and unlike the previous administration, we have made clear that the IHRA Working Definition of Antisemitism, inclusive of its examples, is the only definition this administration supports.

My office was proud to spearhead an interagency effort to arrest Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood Al-Saadi, a radical Islamist who claimed responsibility for multiple attacks and attempted plots throughout Europe earlier this year and who sought to do the same across the Western Hemisphere. “The role of the state,” as President Trump and Secretary Rubio have shown, is an uncompromising one. Now we are urging our partners to follow suit.

When you fight antisemitism, good news is rare. Under Argentina’s presidency, however, real change is taking root across our hemisphere. We congratulate Paraguay for pursuing IHRA membership and thank the Dominican Republic and Peru for endorsing the IHRA Working Definition of Antisemitism, inclusive of its examples, as well. From Colombia to Bolivia, Chile to Costa Rica, and Panama to Guatemala, governments across the region are taking a stand and tackling this scourge.

Beyond our hemisphere, Armenia too has expressed its willingness to join IHRA. We are now finding partners in regions where progress once seemed impossible. As antisemitism fuels violence and terror around the world, governments across the Middle East and North Africa are showing what happens when a state decides to act. Saudi Arabia has addressed concerning themes in textbooks and school curricula; Morocco has expanded Holocaust education in schools and opened a Jewish museum; and the United Arab Emirates participated for the first time ever in the Special Envoys and Coordinators Combating Antisemitism Forum in Dublin just last month.

Yet while these governments make tremendous strides, too many of our European partners are failing to fulfill their commitments to protect Jewish communities. It is shocking that they keep their seats at the table while many of the governments now leading the way remain outside it. Some are prevented from joining — that is a double standard. Others are new to this fight — that is an opportunity.

Once again, too many of our European partners are failing to lead in the way in the fight against hatred. Too many seem satisfied with the status quo — simply checking a box to say “we did it.” After a year of lethal attacks targeting Jewish communities worldwide, none of us can say that the status quo is working. None of us can say that checking a box is working.

Under President Trump and Secretary Rubio, the United States will not simply check a box. We want to see real, decisive change. That is why the United States urges IHRA and other bodies in the fight against antisemitism to build on Argentina’s historic efforts. Rather than gate keep participation, we need to prioritize expanding the global reach of our coalition. Any government that is serious about countering antisemitism, promoting Holocaust remembrance and education, and standing with Jewish communities should have a seat at the table.

Can any European government tell this body that they are fighting hatred better than the Emiratis? Can any government say that Saudi Arabia improving its curricula is not a historic opportunity to expand our coalition against hatred?

The threat is too urgent to turn away allies in this fight.

Since my first day in office as the United States Special Envoy to Monitor and Combat Antisemitism, I have said that every civilized country should be a member of this body. To every government that is not yet an IHRA member, including the many governments from Latin America here today, we urge you: pursue IHRA membership and endorse the IHRA Working Definition of Antisemitism, inclusive of its examples. Together with the Global Guidelines for Countering Antisemitism, these steps show that your government is ready to lead in this fight.

The success of IHRA, or any multilateral body, however, will be measured not in its ability to make commitments. To commit to do something is easy. To check a box is even easier. Our success will be measured only in our ability to implement those commitments. That is why we ask everyone here who already has joined IHRA: are you actually living up to what being a part of this global coalition demands?

If your government has endorsed the IHRA Working Definition of Antisemitism, inclusive of its examples, are you implementing policies that apply “double standards by requiring of [Israel] a behavior not expected or demanded of any other democratic nation”? And if your government is looking to single out Israel, what are you doing to hold the Palestinian Authority accountable for its antisemitic behavior, including promoting Holocaust distortion? What are you doing to ensure it ends pay-for-slay and holds free and fair elections? And what are you doing to ensure Hamas disarms? Whether its rioters burning American and Israeli flags in the streets of France or excessive sanctions regimes in countries like Norway, Israel should not be the scapegoat.

If your government has endorsed the U.S.-led Global Guidelines for Countering Antisemitism, have you adopted a national strategy or action plan and appointed a designated envoy or coordinator with the necessary empowerment and resources to be effective? And as if the issue was not big enough, for how many envoys or coordinators are antisemitism and Holocaust issues just one small part of your other mandates?

And if your government is a participating State of the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe and has endorsed the 2004 Berlin and 2014 Basel declarations, are you collecting and reporting disaggregated antisemitic hate crime data? And if you are collecting that data, are you actually using it to craft your policy response?

The role of the state does not end in making commitments, endorsing definitions, or joining a multilateral body like IHRA. That is where it begins. That is where it starts.

Your responsibility as government officials, envoys and coordinators, IHRA delegates, and community leaders is to lead — to remind your government of its own moral obligations. Leadership is not comfortable. Leadership is not easy. But lead we must.

Allow me to share a brief thought about the rules of kashrut. The definition of a kosher fish is outlined clearly by God in the bible: a fish must have fins and scales. But there is another unwritten requirement — not written in the Bible — which many people forget: a fish found floating on top of the water is not kosher. A kosher fish must be alive when it is caught. It must swim against the stream. Against the current. My fellow government officials, envoys and coordinators, IHRA delegates, and community leaders: the time to swim against the current is now.

Now is not the time to conform to the status quo. To resort to exclusionary mindsets that make no sense. Let us lead. Let us work together with any country that stands with us.

When Hitler rose to power in 1933, we did not have strong leaders like President Trump or President Milei who were ready to confront this evil head-on. We know all too well what happens when real leadership gives way to appeasement, abdication, and complicity.

A government is judged by how it keeps law and order — how it ensures that every citizen is safe and secure. I urge everyone here to ask yourselves: is my government doing all that it can to ensure Jews feel safe in my country? Or can we do better?

As President Trump said last year during the Days of Remembrance, “We declare that never again means now.” Under President Trump and Secretary Rubio, the United States affirms that expanding the frontiers of remembrance cannot and must not end at the conclusion of this plenary. It requires a sustained commitment to expanding the breadth of our global coalition and the depth of our action.

I extend my sincerest gratitude and congratulations to our Argentine hosts and wish everyone a productive plenary. Thank you.

WASHINGTON – Representatives Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03) and Don Bacon (NE-02) recently led a bipartisan effort calling on the Department of State and the Department of Homeland Security to provide urgent answers regarding the conditions and future resettlement plans for Afghan allies and their families currently housed at Camp As Sayliyah (CAS) in Doha, Qatar.
“Our Afghan allies stood alongside us, and we have the responsibility to ensure they and their families are treated with dignity and compassion,” said Rep. Ansari. “These women and children deserve access to medical care, education, and safe living conditions. We must uphold our country’s commitments and ensure these families have a clear path permanent resettlement and asylum. I’m glad to lead this bipartisan effort with my colleague, Congressman Don Bacon, to deliver the answers and accountability our Afghan allies deserve.”
“We made a commitment to the Afghan allies who stood alongside our servicemembers, and we have an obligation to honor it,” said Rep. Bacon. “We need clear answers about the care these families are receiving, particularly women and children, and the steps being taken to ensure their safe and orderly resettlement.”
With Afghan families enduring prolonged stays at CAS, the lawmakers are demanding accountability for the conditions they face and the services available to them. The letter calls for answers on access to essential maternal and OB-GYN care for pregnant women, routine pediatric services for young children, and safe, adequate living conditions. It also urges the provision of structured educational programming, English-language instruction, and recreational activities to support children’s development and well-being. Additionally, the lawmakers demand transparency around proposed third-country transfers, including clear assurances that any agreements uphold U.S. humanitarian standards, protect Afghan families’ well-being, and provide concrete pathways to safe, supported resettlement.
“More than 1,000 Afghan allies are waiting at Camp As Sayliyah, and most of them are women and children. They include family members of U.S. service members, and every one of them was brought there on an American promise. Representatives Ansari and Bacon are asking the right questions: Are pregnant women getting care? Are children learning? Is there a real path to resettlement? These families have kept their word to us, and they deserve clear answers and a way forward. AfghanEvac is grateful to every member who signed on,” said Shawn VanDiver, President and Founder of AfghanEvac.
“Last year, my team and I were at Camp As Sayliyah (CAS) helping secure flights and resettlement for hundreds of our wartime allies. Many of our allies, including the family members of U.S. veterans and service members, are still waiting for a safe path forward and still depend on health care and education at the camp,” said Andrew Sullivan, Executive Director of No One Left Behind. “We applaud this bipartisan recognition that a safe resolution for these allies, reached by Congress and the executive branch working in partnership, is in America’s best interest,” said Andrew Sullivan, Executive Director of No One Left Behind.
Ansari’s letter was cosigned by Representatives Don Bacon (NE-02), Jason Crow (CO-06), María Elvira Salazar (FL-27), Stephen F. Lynch (MA-08), Jasmine Crockett (TX-30), Diana DeGette (CO-01), Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC-AL), Seth Moulton (MA-06), George Latimer (NY-16), James R. Walkinshaw (VA-11), Mike Quigley (IL-05), Adelita S. Grijalva (AZ-07), Ami Bera (CA-06), Deborah K. Ross (NC-02), Julia Brownley (CA-26), Veronica Escobar (TX-16), Emily Randall (WA-06), Jennifer L. McClellan (VA-04), William R. Keating (MA-09), Dina Titus (NV-01), and Sara Jacobs (CA-51).
The letter is also endorsed by One Left Behind, AfghanEvac, Afghans For A Better Tomorrow, Association of Wartime Allies (AWA), FAER, With Honor, USAHello, Center for Gender & Refugee Studies, Borderlands Resource Initiative, Human Rights First, Humanitarian Legal Assistance Project, Special Operations Association of America (SOAA), Refugee Council USA (RCUSA), Lawyers for Good Government, Feminist Majority, Frontera Federation, Keeping Our Promise Inc., Instant Aid, Cross Cultural Communications, LLC, Iraq and Afghanistan Veterans of America, Hearts & Homes for Refugees, Unitarian Universalists for Social Justice, The 5ive Pillars Organization, Allied Shepherd, International Institute of New England, Dialogue Center for Resilience and Empowerment (DCRE), Paws Unite People Inc, SunEx Aviation, Our Culture is Giving, U.S. Committee for Refugees and Immigrants, Asian Americans Advancing Justice Southern California, Afghan Scout Relief Fund, Afghan Advantage, Global Refuge, Union for Reform Judaism, and Immigrant Defenders Law Center.
Read the letter HERE and below.
Dear Secretary Rubio and Secretary Mullin,
We write to follow up on the ongoing transit operations at Camp As Sayliyah (CAS) in Doha, Qatar, where Afghan allies and their families remain in temporary housing awaiting final resettlement processing. In particular, we wish to learn more about the conditions faced by the hundreds of women and the young children currently in processing at the facility, and to request an update on plans for their safe resettlement.
These individuals were brought out of Afghanistan on U.S.-provided flights with the promise and understanding that CAS would serve as a short-term transit hub for temporary stay in the final stages of their processing for secure resettlement to the United States. With this sacred promise to the heroes who supported our forces in Afghanistan at the heart of our inquiry, we want to ensure that the most vulnerable among those at CAS receive the necessary processing support, health care, and clear communications on their next steps.
- Health and Support Services for Women and Children
Given the extended stays for many families, maintaining adequate specialized care remains a priority. We request an assessment of the medical services available at CAS, particularly maternal and OBGYN health resources for pregnant women and routine pediatric care for young children. Ensuring appropriate living conditions and consistent medical oversight for these families is essential as their immigration processing moves forward.
- Educational Opportunities and Developmental Support for Children
Beyond immediate health and security considerations, we also ask for an evaluation of the educational and developmental resources available to the school-aged children residing at CAS. Given the extended length of stay for many families, access to structured educational programming, English language learning, and recreational activities is essential to minimize learning disruptions and support childhood development. Ensuring there are routine learning environments at the facility not only helps prepare these children for integration into American schools and communities, but also provides critical stability and psychological support during a period of prolonged transition.
- Pathways to Final Resettlement
Clear and transparent communication regarding resettlement pathways is vital for maintaining the trust of our allies now and in future engagements. We ask for clarification on the open U.S. Refugee Admissions Program (USRAP) P-1/P-2 applications and family reunification cases at CAS. Additionally, we request information on how the Department of State and the Department of Homeland Security are handling any proposed third-country transfers to ensure the underlying bilateral agreements align with U.S. humanitarian standards and provide established resettlement support in the receiving country.
To inform Congress’ collaboration with your departments to shape an effective path forward, we
request your response addressing the following questions by November 27, 2026:
- What medical care is available for the Afghan evacuees at CAS, particularly maternal and OBGYN health resources for pregnant women and routine pediatric care for young children?
- What learning support is available to school aged children? What cultural and educational resources are available to prepare adults for employment and resettlement in the United States?
- How many individuals have ongoing USRAP referrals? What resources do your departments need to ensure all these individuals can renew their requisite documents and medical panels?
- What specific steps are your departments taking to communicate the status of resettlement options (including USRAP and third country agreements) to the individuals at CAS?
Thank you for your continued work to uphold U.S. national security by fulfilling our commitments to Afghan allies and their families. We look forward to working with your departments to ensure a swift, safe, and organized resolution for those at CAS.
Sincerely,
Yassamin Ansari
Member of Congress
Follow @RepYassAnsari on all social media platforms and visit Ansari.House.gov to learn more.
###
title: Ansari Leads Bipartisan Effort in Demanding Answers on Care and Resettlement of Afghan Women and Children in Qatar

CINCINNATI – In keeping with past practice, United States Attorney Dominick S. Gerace II announced today that he has designated Election Officers in each of the District’s three offices to serve as points of contact for the upcoming election.

“The Department of Justice plays an important role in ensuring that our elections are free and fair,” said Gerace. “My Office will always work to protect the integrity of the election process.”

U.S. Attorney Gerace appointed:

Deputy Criminal Chief Emily N. Glatfelter in Cincinnati;

Assistant United States Attorney Peter K. Glenn-Applegate in Columbus; and

Deputy Criminal Chief Brent G. Tabacchi in Dayton.

As District Election Officers, they are responsible for overseeing the District’s handling of complaints of election fraud and voting rights concerns in consultation with the Justice Department’s Headquarters in Washington.

The Department's long-standing Election Day Program seeks to ensure public confidence in the integrity of the election process by providing local contacts for the public to report possible election fraud and voting rights violations.

Federal law protects against such crimes as non-citizen voting, intimidating or bribing voters, buying and selling votes, impersonating voters, altering vote tallies, stuffing ballot boxes, and marking ballots for voters against their wishes or without their input. It also contains special protections for the rights of voters and provides that they can vote free from acts that intimidate or harass them.

The local FBI field office can be reached by the public regarding allegations of election fraud and other election abuses at 1-800-CALL-FBI.

Complaints about possible violations of the federal voting rights laws can be made directly to the Civil Rights Division in Washington, DC by phone at 800-253-3931 or by complaint form at https://civilrights.justice.gov/ .

# # #
title: U.S. Attorney Gerace announces District Election Officers

PICATINNY ARSENAL, N.J. - Engineers at the U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command (DEVCOM) Armaments Center researchers say a new explosive initiator could remove environmental and safety risks from the supply chain.
DBX-1, full name copper (I) 5-nitrotetrazolate, provides the U.S. Military with an alternative to lead azide, used for decades because of its military reliability despite known risks to human health due to its volatility and toxic composition. DBX-1 maintains a lower toxicity than its legacy counterpart, is more efficient to manufacture and transport and supports a modernized supply chain with no compromise to weapon production or reliability.
As a copper-based compound, DBX-1 eliminates exposure risk to lead while handling, and at the same time opens an avenue towards automation. Instead of a dry powder, DBX-1 is prepared as a wet slurry and is dispensed into initiators via automated equipment, ensuring no dry handling and significantly reducing worker contact with sensitive primary explosives.
Lead azide has been a ubiquitous compound in explosives for decades, mostly used as the initiator in an explosive train, found at the heart of most armaments. Initiators are the first materials in the train, converting a trigger into a reliable detonation that sets off the rest of the sequence.
Lead azide and similar compounds like lead styphnate work well as initiators, but they come with significant caveats – lead is highly toxic, and due to supply chain disruptions and a limited domestic manufacturer base, warfighters must rely on aged stockpiles and single source suppliers for initiation and ignition. Lead azide, according to the National Institute of Health, produces toxic fumes when set alight, and is highly sensitive to heat, friction and impact when dry.
However, as these compounds are highly effective in the field, interests in finding alternatives have historically been muted. Lead azide only requires a small stimulus to trigger a large blast and does so consistently.
According to Senior Lead Chemical Engineer Neha Mehta, the DBX-1 project started from a desire to find a drop-in replacement to lead azide and similar compounds, which evolved into the pursuit of an azide alternative over time. The Primary Explosives and Detonator Lab Team encountered DBX-1 while at a primary explosive workshop, being presented by Pacific Scientific, said Mehta. The team was captivated by promises of lower toxicity, safer handling and strong energetic output, and several years of rigorous testing have thoroughly validated those beliefs.
“We did a lot of in‑house testing, and aside from a couple small confusions, we had zero no‑go’s. We’re always optimizing, always looking for how to make things better. Our goal has never been to change the hardware; we work with what already exists,” she explained.
DBX‑1 is fully sourced and produced within the United States, thus strengthening availability, providing a manufacturing base at home and mitigating supply disruption. Testing is ongoing in different applications, but so far, the compound has performed well across detonators, some primers, and fuze configurations, including anti-personnel obstacle breaching systems and grenade and artillery fuzes. It has also proved reliability across the Army’s smallest commonly used stab detonator (M55) and its largest (C70).
“If we can prove it in the smallest detonator and the largest detonator, everything in between will work, and that’s exactly what we’ve shown,” noted Mehta.
The team has already exhibited DBX‑1 as an alternative to lead azide and lead styphnate by completing the full fuze qualification test matrix for an artillery fuze, funded by the Safer Alternative for Readiness – Airborne Lead Reduction (SAFR ALR) and the Project Manager Combat Ammunition Systems. They also proved DBX‑1’s suitability for grenade fuzes, successfully finishing the full performance tests and mini‑arena evaluation of complete grenades equipped with a toxic‑free delay, lead‑free primer and lead‑free detonator, funded by Environmental Security Technology Certification Program (ESTCP).
The program has conducted extensive test series across numerous electric blasting‑cap configurations using the Army Remote Activation Munitions System and has met all its operational requirements. DBX-1 has also cleared qualification for tactical breaching initiators and point-detonating artillery fuzing systems.
According to lead mechanical engineering technicians Jason Semanek and John Marin, DBX-1 required not only laboratory success but also demonstrating manufacturability. Rocky Mountain Scientific Laboratory, based in Colorado with a growing facility in Texas, is positioned to manufacture DBX‑1. Innovative Materials and Processes in South Dakota, under Army contract, is developing the automated slurry‑loading process, while Action Manufacturing in Pennsylvania assisted in optimizing precursor synthesis, providing a significant boost to American manufacturing.
Additionally, both the DBX-1 manufacturing process and its automated loading equipment are being designed to operate inside transportable Conex containers. This means no need for dedicated permanent buildings, streamlines site approvals and reduces transportation risks, along with further simplifying stockpiling logistics. DBX-1 had its pre-pilot testing finished in 2025 and its full-scale pilot plant should be ready by the end of 2027 or early 2028, where it will be produced on-demand.
Mehta stated that funding for DBX-1 has been inconsistent, thus complicating the testing required to validate it across dozens of munition systems. She gave thanks to the SAFR program for giving the team financial support continuously, to the ESTCP, Army ManTech, the OSW’s Manufacturing Science and Technology Program and project managers for support and to the rest of her team for its dedication in helping ensure project success.
Despite its lengthy timeline, the team expressed pride and excitement over the program’s progress, noting that a few outside organizations have shown interest in DBX-1, particularly in mining. For the engineers, seeing DBX‑1 move toward full qualification and adoption feels like guiding a long-developed project into maturity, one they hope will be fully integrated across military systems within the near future.
“It’s like a child - slow progress, lots of work and now it’s finally ready to go out into the world,” quipped Marin.
title: A new class of blast: DBX 1 compound pushing Army towards cleaner, smarter firepower

FORT GEORGE G. MEADE, Md. — Baltimore Ravens players, former players and cheerleaders visited Fort George G. Meade Oct. 27, giving service members an opportunity to interact with professional athletes while highlighting the importance of military service, community partnerships and quality of life.
The visit, coordinated through a partnership involving the National Football League, USAA and Fort Meade’s Directorate of Family and Morale, Welfare and Recreation, included a military working dog demonstration and an autograph and photo session.
Command Sgt. Maj. Richard Moore welcomed the Ravens delegation at the installation’s Visitor Control Center before escorting the group to the military working dog kennels.
At the kennels, Lt. Col. Heather George, Headquarters Command Battalion commander, welcomed the visitors and introduced the military working dog team. The delegation received a briefing on the dogs’ training, capabilities and role in supporting military operations before watching a demonstration.
“The Baltimore Ravens visit provided a tremendous opportunity to showcase the professionalism, training and capabilities of our military working dog teams while strengthening the connection between our service members and the community,” George said.
Following the demonstration, Moore presented Ravens representatives with an American flag flown here that same day in appreciation for their visit and support of the military community.
The delegation then traveled to the Freedom Inn Warrior Restaurant, where service members met Ravens players, took photographs and collected autographs.
“Seeing the excitement and enthusiasm of our service members as they interacted with the Baltimore Ravens was truly rewarding,” said Command Sgt. Maj. Karen Bryant. “These engagements go beyond autographs and photographs. They help build morale, strengthen camaraderie and remind our Soldiers that the community values their service and sacrifices.”
For Staff Sgt. Lamar Riddick, the opportunity to meet professional athletes was a meaningful acknowledgment of military service.
“I think it shows great appreciation,” Riddick said. “It makes me feel valued.”
Pfc. Jaydon Green, a Ravens fan, shared that excitement. After learning about the visit, he immediately contacted his wife and made plans to attend.
“It feels like I’m respected,” Green said. “It feels like some of the service that we do here is kind of makes us feel like we get a little bit back from it.”
For former Ravens wide receiver Torrey Smith, whose father served in the military, the visit carried personal significance.
“I think it’s important to know that people matter, right? And that you appreciate them,” Smith said. “It’s a major sacrifice. It’s a major commitment that so many people make.”
Moore said the engagement highlighted the shared values of military service and professional athletics.
“Collaborating with world-class organizations like the Baltimore Ravens powerfully highlights our shared ethos,” Moore said. “We are both driven by core values and the relentless pursuit of excellence.”
The visit reinforced Fort Meade’s commitment to supporting service member morale, strengthening community relationships and providing opportunities to recognize the dedication and sacrifice of military personnel and their families.
title: Baltimore Ravens visit Fort Meade service members

Media accreditation is open for the next launch to deliver NASA science investigations, supplies, and equipment to the International Space Station. A Northrop Grumman Cygnus XL spacecraft will launch in November to the orbital laboratory on a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket for NASA.
The mission is known as NASA’s Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Services 25, or NASA’s Northrop Grumman CRS-25. Liftoff is targeted for no earlier than 10:49 a.m. EST, Sunday, Nov. 29, from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida.
Following launch, astronauts aboard the space station will use the Canadarm2 robotic arm to capture Cygnus and install the spacecraft to the Unity module’s Earth-facing port for cargo unloading. The spacecraft will remain at the space station until May 2027. This is the company’s 25th spacecraft built to deliver supplies to the International Space Station under contract with NASA.
Credentialing to cover prelaunch and launch activities is open to U.S. media. The application deadline for U.S. citizens is 11:59 p.m. EST, Thursday, Nov. 12. All accreditation requests must be submitted online at:
Credentialed media will receive a confirmation email following approval. NASA’s media accreditation policy is available online. For questions about accreditation, or to request special logistical support, email: ksc-media-accreditat@mail.nasa.gov. For other questions, please contact NASA’s Kennedy Space Center newsroom at: 321-867-2468.
In addition to food, supplies, and equipment for the crew, Cygnus will deliver several new experiments, including hardware to manufacture tiny, DNA-inspired particles in space that could improve drug delivery for cancer and osteoarthritis, as well as a study that could guide cancer treatments by predicting whether a patient’s cancer is likely to spread to other parts of the body. Cygnus also will carry human muscle cells and medications to test therapeutics for muscle loss associated with spaceflight and aging on Earth, and a compact radiation sensor designed to improve crew safety on future missions.
Each resupply mission to the station delivers scientific investigations in the areas of biology and biotechnology, Earth and space science, physical sciences, and technology development and demonstrations. Cargo resupply from U.S. companies ensures a national capability to deliver scientific research to the space station, increasing NASA’s ability to conduct new investigations aboard humanity’s laboratory in space.
For 26 years, people have lived and worked continuously aboard the International Space Station, advancing scientific knowledge and making research breakthroughs that are not possible on Earth. The space station is an important testbed for NASA to understand and overcome the challenges of long-duration spaceflight and to expand commercial opportunities in low Earth orbit. As commercial companies concentrate on providing human space transportation services and destinations as part of a strong low Earth orbit economy, NASA is focusing its resources on deep space missions to the Moon as part of the Artemis and Moon Base programs to build on our foundation for the first astronaut missions to Mars.

Today, the Department of State signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the United Parcel Service (UPS). Through this MoU, the Department of State and UPS will leverage UPS’s unrivaled logistics network, cargo transportation, and supply chain expertise in support of Department of State-led disaster response efforts around the world – helping deliver life-saving assistance faster and more effectively.

When disasters strike, speed and reach save lives. This partnership with UPS brings the best of American private sector logistics capability to bear alongside the Department of State’s disaster response expertise. Lofgren Secures Over $54 Million for Pajaro River Flood Protection As El Niño Is Expected to Strengthen
WATSONVILLE, CA — Today, Congresswoman Zoe Lofgren (CA-18) delivered a $54,830,000 check for the Pajaro River Flood Risk Management Project, one of her 13 community projects she submitted for the Fiscal Year 2026 congressional appropriations cycle. This is the largest single community project that Lofgren secured this year, which is being completed by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) San Francisco District, in partnership with the Pajaro Regional Flood Management Agency (PRFMA). Senators Alex Padilla (D-CA) and Adam Schiff (D-CA) also requested congressional funding for this project.
“With El Niño expected to intensify in the early months of 2027, it’s critical that the residents and businesses along the Pajaro River have necessary flood protection,” said Rep. Lofgren. “Last year, I was proud to announce nearly $40 million for levee and floodwall construction in Watsonville, and I’m proud to have submitted this additional $54 million as one of my community projects this year. That’s going to help save lives and property, and I’m proud to have worked with Senators Padilla and Schiff to prioritize this project funding.”
“Consistent funding for the Pajaro River flood control project is critically important, and we are grateful to Rep. Lofgren for her work to keep the project moving forward and fulfilling our commitments to the vulnerable residents and businesses in the Pajaro Valley,” said Mark Strudley, Executive Director of PRFMA.
“Future improvements to the levee will make a real difference in reducing flood risks and protecting the people who call Watsonville and the Pajaro Valley home,” said Watsonville City Manager Tamara Vides. This is an investment in the safety, stability, and future of our community. We are thankful for the advocacy and support provided by Congresswoman Lofgren.”
The residents and businesses of Watsonville and Pajaro have been waiting for 50 years for flood protection and during that time have suffered significant damage and loss of life due to weather events. On March 11, 2023, a serious levee failure resulted in the evacuation of more than 2,000 people in the Town of Pajaro, 200 water rescues, significant flooding of farms, and closure of Highway 1. The farms impacted by flooding are vital contributors to the regional agricultural industry, where none of the fruit and vegetable crops are federally subsidized and floods can result in the loss of 2-3 growing seasons.
According to the National Weather Service, El Niño continues to strengthen with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027. Lofgren has urged Californians to prepare for storm season and sign up for emergency alerts. Tips and resources for El Niño can be viewed on her website.
Rep. Lofgren’s community project submissions this year have delivered a total of $58,022,000 for Watsonville and Santa Cruz County. This includes $1.2 million to renovate the Watsonville Veterans Hall, $1,092,000 to replace Watsonville’s wastewater infrastructure, and $900,000 for the Sí Se Puede Behavioral Health Center.
title: Lofgren Secures Over $54 Million for Pajaro River Flood Protection As El Niño Is Expected to Strengthen

Fort Myers, Florida – Angel Rey Rivera (35, Fort Myers) was sentenced today by U.S. District Judge Kyle Dudek to five years in federal prison to be followed by 3 years of supervised release for possessing a firearm as a convicted felon. Rivera pleaded guilty on July 28, 2026. United States Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe made the announcement.

According to court records, Rivera was captured on video throwing a stolen firearm into a trash can after fleeing from officers from the Fort Myers Police Department on Palm Beach Boulevard. Upon arrest, Rivera exclaimed, “I don’t care about none of that. I already did 11 years. I’ll go lay down again.” Rivera had recently been released from the Tennessee Department of Corrections after serving nearly 11 years for multiple felony convictions, including two counts of attempted second-degree murder and attempted aggravated robbery.

This case was investigated by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives and the Fort Myers Police Department. It was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Matthew Redavid.

This case is part of Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) – the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities.

The information filed against Hawa alleges that, during this May 16, 2026, visit to the Liberty Bell Center, she flicked an oily substance over the barrier protecting the Liberty Bell. The substance hit and remained on the Liberty Bell and surrounding areas.

If convicted, Gerlach faces a maximum of one year in prison and Hawa faces a maximum of six months in prison.

This case was investigated by the FBI and the National Park Service.

Homeland Security Task Force: Two Connecticut Men Found with 21 Kilos of Cocaine Sentenced to 10 Years in Federal Prison
BRIDGEPORT, Conn. - David X. Sullivan, United States Attorney for the District of Connecticut, today announced that REGINALD ROGERS 38, of Woodbridge, and LESTER ARRINGTON, 34, of Naugatuck, have each been sentenced by U.S. District Judge Stefan R. Underhill in Bridgeport to 120 months of imprisonment and five years of supervised release for trafficking cocaine. Rogers was sentenced today and Arrington was sentenced on October 27.
According to court documents and statements made in court, as part of a Homeland Security Task Force investigation, on February 23, 2026, Connecticut State Police troopers stopped a 2024 Subaru Crosstrek in Trumbull. Rogers was driving the vehicle and Arrington was a passenger. A K9 sniff of the vehicle alerted for the presence of narcotics, and a subsequent search revealed approximately 21 kilograms of cocaine hidden in two compartments (“traps”) that were installed under each front seat. Rogers and Arrington were arrested on state charges at that time.
Rogers and Arrington each pleaded guilty to possession with intent to distribute five kilograms or more of cocaine. Each is released on a $150,000 bond and they are required to report to prison on January 13.
Arrington and Rogers agreed to the forfeiture of the vehicle.
This investigation was led by the Drug Enforcement Administration with the assistance of the Bridgeport, Danbury, Stamford, and Stratford Police Departments. The case was prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Justyn P. Stokely and Lauren C. Clark.
This prosecution is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement toward identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders.
